item.title: 腾讯开源 DFly2：共享目标稀疏 KV Cache 的创新投机解码技术
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-28/腾讯开源-DFly2-投机解码框架/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-28/腾讯开源-DFly2-投机解码框架/
item.description:
在大语言模型 (Large Language Model, LLM) 的实际部署与长文本推理中，传统的投机解码 (Speculative Decoding) 虽然能显著提升生成速度，但往往需要让辅助草稿模型 (Drafter) 独立维护一份庞大的键值缓存 (KV Cache)，导致长上下文和高并发场景下的显存开销居高不下。为了攻克这一瓶颈，Tencent 旗下混元 AI Infra 团队正式开源了全新块级并行投机解码框架 **DFly2**。该框架专门面向原生稀疏的大语言模型设计，革命性地直接复用目标模型的隐层 KV Cache 和稀疏索引结果，彻底甩掉了草稿模型的独立显存包袱，将草稿解码计算复杂度与上下文长度解耦。基准测试结果表明，DFly2 在 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、GLM-5.3-Flash 及 Tencent 自研的 Hy4 flash 等主流模型上均实现了更高的草稿接受率，并在长上下文智能体任务中实现了高达 81% 的服务吞吐量跃升，为超长文本模型的高性能低成本推理树立了全新标杆。
---
## 概述
> ## Summary
Tencent 正式[开源了 DFly2](https://x.com/TencentAI_News/status/2125968859450802415)。这是一款创新的块级并行投机解码草稿模型 (Drafter)，专为原生稀疏架构的大语言模型 (Large Language Model, LLM) 打造，完美支持 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、GLM-5.3-Flash 以及 Tencent 自研的 [Hy4 flash](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-flash) 等模型。DFly2 巧妙地摒弃了草稿模型独立的键值缓存 (KV Cache)，转而直接共享目标模型的隐层 KV Cache 与稀疏索引器筛选结果，大幅削减了显存开销，不仅能支持更高的并发请求，还在长文本以及智能体任务中实现了高达 **81% 的吞吐量提升**。
> Tencent has [open-sourced DFly2](https://x.com/TencentAI_News/status/2125968859450802415), an innovative block-parallel speculative decoding drafter designed specifically for natively sparse Large Language Models (LLMs) such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, GLM-5.3-Flash, and Tencent's own [Hy4 flash](https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hy4-flash). By cleverly eliminating the need for a separate draft KV cache—instead sharing the target model's latent KV cache and sparse indexer picks—DFly2 drastically reduces memory overhead, enabling higher concurrency and up to an **81% throughput increase** on long-context and agentic tasks.
---
## 核心速览 (TL;DR)
> ## TL;DR
* **模型规模**：为 Hy4 flash 配套推出的草稿模型参数量为 0.85B (8.5 亿参数)，包含 5 个网络层。 * **硬件环境**：在线服务测试基于搭载 vLLM 的 NVIDIA H20 GPU 展开 (单实例采用 TP8 张量并行)；vLLM 官方推荐配置默认面向 8 张 H200。 * **整体性能**：在所有测试的目标模型以及通用基准测试中，相比相同训练配方的 DFlash 与 DSpark，DFly2 均取得了更高的草稿接受率。 * **最佳表现**：在用户级解码速度持平的前提下，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 在 64K 上下文的 SWE 代码基准测试中吞吐量提升高达 81%。 * **最小收益**：在 temperature 为 0 的常规任务下，DFly2 相比 DSpark 在 Hy4 flash 上的性能提升幅度最小，为 3.9%。
> * **Size:** 0.85B-parameter, 5-layer drafter shipped with Hy4 flash. > * **Hardware:** Serving tests utilized NVIDIA H20 GPUs with vLLM (TP8 per instance); default vLLM recipes target 8x H200. > * **Performance:** Higher draft acceptance rates compared to same-recipe DFlash and DSpark across all target models and general benchmarks. > * **Best Results:** Up to 81% more throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (SWE 64K) at matched per-user speed. > * **Smallest Gains:** 3.9% improvement over DSpark on Hy4 flash general tasks at temperature 0.
---
## 什么是 DFly2？
> ## What is DFly2?
DFly2 是由 Tencent 混元 AI Infra 团队研发的块级并行投机解码草稿模型，相关成果详见学术论文[《DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target’s Sparsity》](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34776)。
> DFly2 is a block-parallel speculative decoding drafter developed by Tencent’s Hunyuan AI Infra team, detailed in the research paper [‘DFly2: Turbocharging Long-Context Speculative Decoding by Sharing the Target’s Sparsity’](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.34776).
标准的投机解码技术通过引入轻量级辅助模型 (草稿模型) 预先生成候选 Token，再由大体积的目标模型通过单次前向传播进行批量验证，在确保输出完全无损的前提下成倍加快生成速度。然而在长上下文应用场景中，这一方案的成本却急剧攀升：因为传统草稿模型不仅必须对整个前文字符串执行注意力计算，还必须单独开辟并维护一份专属于自己的 KV Cache。
> Standard speculative decoding utilizes a small auxiliary model (drafter) to propose tokens while the larger target model verifies them in a single pass, ensuring the output remains entirely lossless. However, in long-context scenarios, this approach becomes costly because traditional drafters must attend over the entire prefix and maintain their own separate KV cache.
---
## DFly2 的工作原理是什么？
> ## How Does DFly2 Work?
DFly2 将草稿模型的每一层与目标模型中的稀疏注意力层进行一对一直接配对，实现了两项核心关键组件的共享：
> DFly2 pairs each draft layer directly with a sparse attention layer in the target model, sharing two key components:
* **KV 共享 (KV Sharing)**：草稿层直接读取与其配对的目标模型层的隐层 KV Cache。 * **索引共享 (Index Sharing)**：草稿层仅对目标模型稀疏索引器已选定的位置执行注意力计算 (即 top-$k$ 稀疏 KV)。 * **权重初始化 (Initialization)**：每个草稿层均直接使用配对目标层的权重进行初始化。 * **隐藏状态注入 (Hidden Injection)**：目标模型最后一层的隐藏状态通过门控机制注入到草稿块中。 * **块内校正 (Intra-Block Correction)**：草稿模型在一个候选块内逐槽位重新读取共享的上下文信息。
> * **KV Sharing:** The draft layer reads the paired target layer’s latent KV cache directly. > * **Index Sharing:** It attends exclusively to positions already selected by the target’s sparse indexer (top-$k$ sparse KV). > * **Initialization:** Each draft layer is initialized using its paired target layer’s weights. > * **Hidden Injection:** The target's last-layer hidden state is gated into the draft block. > * **Intra-Block Correction:** The drafter rereads the shared context slot-by-slot within a block.
根据 [AngelSpec GitHub 开源主页](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec)的介绍，每一个草稿 Token 最多仅关注约 2,000 个 Key 向量，这使得无论上下文长度如何延伸，草稿生成的计算成本都基本保持平稳。此外，DFly2 完全跳过了 Prefill 预填充阶段，这意味着从 Prefill 切换至 Decode 解码阶段时，仅仅需要额外传递一个最后一层的隐藏状态。
> According to the [AngelSpec GitHub page](https://github.com/Tencent/AngelSpec), each draft token attends to at most ~2K keys, keeping drafting costs roughly flat regardless of context length. Furthermore, DFly2 skips prefill entirely, meaning the prefill-to-decode transfer only adds a single last-layer hidden state.
---
## 显存开销对比分析：独立缓存 vs. 共享缓存
> ## Memory Cost Analysis: Separate vs. Shared Cache
常规的 3 层草稿模型缓存会在每个 Token 上带来显著的额外显存负担 (以 bf16 数据类型计算，数据源自论文表 2)：
> A conventional 3-layer drafter cache adds significant memory overhead per token (bf16, based on paper Table 2):
| 目标模型 (Target Model) | 目标模型 KV (Target KV) | 草稿缓存 (Drafter Cache) | 显存增加倍数 (Increase Factor) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** | 4.4 KiB | 3.4 KiB | 1.76x | | **GLM-5.3-Flash** | 11.7 KiB | 3.0 KiB | 1.26x | | **Hy4 flash** | 17.2 KiB | 3.4 KiB | 1.20x |
在 32K 上下文长度下，彻底省去草稿模型的专用缓存后，显存池能够容纳的**并发请求数量提升了 1.73 倍**。
> At a 32K context length, removing the drafter's dedicated cache allows the memory pool to accommodate **1.73x more concurrent requests**.
---
## DFly2 基准测试：接受率、加速比与吞吐量
> ## DFly2 Benchmarks: Acceptance, Speedup, and Throughput
*注：所有基准测试数据均为 Tencent 自测公布，基线对比项采用了基于相同配方重新训练的 DFlash 和 DSpark。*
> *All benchmark metrics are self-reported by Tencent, using DFlash and DSpark retrained on identical recipes as baselines.*

item.title: Opus 5.5 与 Fable 5.2 实战：借助 AI 智能体将过度优化的 Rust 代码推向硬件极限
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-28/Opus-5.5-与-Fable-5.2-极致优化-Rust-代码实战/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-28/Opus-5.5-与-Fable-5.2-极致优化-Rust-代码实战/
item.description: 在追求极致性能的系统级软件工程领域，代码优化往往伴随着边际收益递减的巨大挑战。知名数据科学家与工程师 Max Woolf 在前期的实验中，探索了利用大语言模型 (Large Language Model, LLM) 驱动的 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 持续迭代并优化 Rust 代码的流程。随着 Anthropic 全新发布的 **Claude Opus 5.5** 与 **Fable 5.2** 相继亮相，作者将基准测试与性能调优工作流推向了全新的高度——不仅引入了基于 `samply` 的全进程性能剖析与内存占用精简，更创造性地下发底层汇编反思指令，借助 `objdump` 深入编译二进制产物寻找冗余指令与分支。令人瞩目的是，AI 智能体成功在原本已经处于前沿水平的高度优化 Rust 库上，再次实现了 1.5 倍至 2.0 倍的性能飞跃，不仅让峰值内存大幅缩减，更直接促成了极速文本检索工具 `byteseek` 的提前开源，为探索生成式 AI 辅助系统级极致性能优化树立了全新标杆。 --- ## 概要 > ## Summary 在前期利用智能体化大语言模型 (Large Language Model, LLM) 进行代码优化的实验基础之上，作者在一系列高性能 Rust 代码库中对最新发布的 **Claude Opus 5.5** 与 **Fable 5.2** 进行了深入测试。通过从 Codex 切换至 Claude Code，并引入更为激进的工作流——包括使用 `samply` 进行进程性能剖析、大幅精简内存占用、借助 `objdump` 进行汇编指令级审查，以及建立极其严苛的视觉保真度检验机制——这些模型将本已处于业界顶尖水平（State-of-the-Art）的 Rust 软件推向了硬件极限。经过优化后的代码库取得了显著的运行提速（在原有高度优化成果上普遍再提升 1.5 至 2 倍），显著降低了峰值内存占用，并直接催生了一款高性能 grep 替代工具 **byteseek** 的提前开源。 > Building on previous experiments with agentic LLMs for code optimization, the author tests the newly released **Claude Opus 5.5** and **Fable 5.2** on a suite of high-performance Rust libraries. By shifting from Codex to Claude Code and introducing aggressive workflows—such as process profiling with `samply`, memory footprint reduction, assembly-level inspection via `objdump`, and rigorous visual fidelity checks—the models pushed already state-of-the-art Rust software to new extremes. The resulting libraries achieve significant speedups (often 1.5x to 2x beyond previous optimizations), lower peak memory, and even inspired the early open-sourcing of a high-performance grep alternative called **byteseek**. --- ## 从 Codex 切换到 Claude Code > ## Switching from Codex to Claude Code 我喜欢飞快的软件，尤其是那种快到极致的软件。几个月前，我发表了一篇题为《[让智能体优化代码，编写出超越业界前沿水平的高性能 Rust 库](https://minimaxir.com/2026/09/agentic-iteration/)》的博客。在那篇文章中，我列举了利用 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 大语言模型来加速 Rust 软件运行时执行的技巧——当然，其间引入了大量的制衡与核验机制，以确保代码质量良好、防止功能退化，并杜绝大模型在基准测试 (Benchmark) 中弄虚作假。经过足够轮次的迭代后，最终产出的 Rust 代码库不仅在性能上超越了现有的顶尖实现，且功能相同甚至更强，即便对比那些本身就用 Rust 编写的高性能项目亦毫不逊色。当时阻碍我正式开源这些 Rust 代码包（crate）的主要瓶颈有两个：一是需要进行全面严苛的真实场景测试，以确保代码完全如宣传的那般稳定；二是我不想刚把代码开源，随后新发布的大模型转眼就能再找出 2 倍以上的提速空间——那可太让人尴尬了。 > I like fast software. I like *very* fast software. A couple months ago, I published a blog post titled [Writing Rust code that’s faster than state-of-the-art libraries by asking agents to make the code faster](https://minimaxir.com/2026/09/agentic-iteration/) in which I listed techniques for using agentic LLMs to speed up the runtime execution of Rust software—of course, with extensive checks and balances to ensure good code quality, avoid regressions, and mitigate cheating by the LLMs. After enough iterations, the resulting Rust libraries are faster than existing state-of-the-art implementations with the same or better capabilities, even against those already written in Rust. The main bottlenecks for me open-sourcing the resulting Rust crates are a) doing comprehensive real-world testing to ensure the code works as advertised and b) I don’t want to release the code and then have another model release immediately find another 2x-or-more speed boost because that would be embarrassing. 仅仅做到比业界顶尖库更快并不能让我满足：我希望自己的代码能触碰硬件本身的极限，哪怕这只是些可能根本不需要极高吞吐量的“好玩”软件。我不希望自己的基准测试单位还在以毫秒（ms）为单位计算，该死，我希望它们能精准到**微秒（μs）**！谁知道未来的某些应用场景，会不会真的需要亚毫秒级的词云生成或亚毫秒级的 ASCII 字符画渲染呢？ > I’m not satisfied with my code merely being faster than state-of-the-art: I want my code to push against hardware limits even for “fun” software that may not require maximum throughput. I don’t want my benchmarks to be measured in milliseconds, I want them measured in *microseconds*, dammit. Who knows if some application in the future will require submillisecond word clouds or submillisecond ASCII art generations? 在那篇博客中，我的智能体迭代流水线主要使用的是 OpenAI 的 GPT 系列模型。然而就在文章发布的第二天，Anthropic 正式发布了 [Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5)。鉴于先前的 Opus 5 表现平平，外界起初对此充满怀疑……但事实很快证明，Opus 5.5 在智能体能力上实现了跨越式的代际跃升，能够从容解决无论是 OpenAI 还是 Anthropic 其他模型都无法攻克的高难度技术任务。在目睹社区的轰动后，我每月花费 20 美元把 Opus 5.5 接入到自己的智能体迭代流水线中进行测试……仅仅过了两天，其卓越的表现就彻底折服了我，促使我毫不犹豫地升级到了每月 100 美元的订阅档位以获取更多使用额度。经过过去几个月的深入测试，我可以充满信心地断言：Opus 5.5 以及随后推出的孪生模型 Fable 5.2，确实带来了重大的性能突破，真正将我的 Rust 软件推向了硬件极限。 > In that blog post, I mostly used OpenAI’s GPT models for this agentic iteration pipeline. The day after publication, Anthropic announced [Claude Opus 5.5](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5), which was met with skepticism as Opus 5 was underwhelming…and then it quickly turned out that Opus 5.5 was a step-change increase in the capability of agents with the ability to complete difficult technical tasks that neither OpenAI’s nor Anthropic’s other models could complete. I spent the $20/mo to try out Opus 5.5 on my agentic iteration pipeline after observing the hype…and after only two days, the results were impressive enough that I paid the $100/mo to get more usage quota. Through more testing over the past couple months, I can confidently say Opus 5.5 and its subsequent Fable 5.2 sibling did in fact result in significant performance breakthroughs that indeed push my Rust software to its limits. 为了避免被大家误以为这是一篇没有标注赞助的 Anthropic 商业软广，我想先说明：在 Opus 5.5 问世之前，我对 [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) 满腹怨气，而这恰恰是我当时转投 OpenAI [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/) 阵营的首要原因。一个典型例子就是，Claude 此前一直无视行业通用的 [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/)，偏偏执拗地强制要求使用 [CLAUDE.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memor)（[直到最近才终于做出调整](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49760187)）——坦白讲，这种自立门槛的小家子气做法足以让人倒戈。 > Lest people think that this post is an undisclosed #ad for Anthropic, I had grievances with [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) prior to Opus 5.5 which were the primary reasons I switched to OpenAI’s [Codex](https://openai.com/codex/). One such example is Claude ignoring [AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/) in favor of [CLAUDE.md](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memor) ([until very recently](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49760187)), which was honestly petty enough to tip the scales. 使用 Claude Code 最让人头疼的问题在于如何选择运行载体（harness）——或者说，根本没得选。尽管在 Opus 4.5 的美好旧时光里，在终端里直接跑 Claude Code 尚可接受，但 Codex 支持任意运行宿主的特性（例如 [Zed Agent](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/zed-agent)，能直接原生调用 Codex 订阅）让开发者能在一个地方井井有条地搞定所有事情。相比之下，Claude Code 却[出了名地](https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-cracks-down-on-unauthorized-claude-usage-by-third-party-harnesses)封杀第三方运行环境，并不遗余力地封堵一切试图绕过限制接入的变通方案。 > The main grievance with using Claude Code is deciding which harness to use—or, rather, the lack of decision. Although I was fine with using Claude Code in the terminal back in the halcyon days of Opus 4.5, Codex’s ability to use any harness, such as [Zed Agent](https://zed.dev/docs/ai/zed-agent) which allows using the Codex subscription natively, made it more convenient to keep everything in one place. In contrast, Claude Code [infamously](https://venturebeat.com/technology/anthropic-cracks-down-on-unauthorized-claude-usage-by-third-party-harnesses) blocks third-party harnesses and has closed workarounds used to access it regardless. 因此，我不得不思考如何在不伤筋动骨改动智能体迭代管线的前提下，找到使用 Opus 5.5 的折中路径。Zed Agent 虽然提供了一个遵循[智能体客户端协议（Agent Client Protocol）](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/introduction)的[变通途径以接入 Claude Code](https://zed.dev/acp/agent/claude-agent)，但由于 Claude 的独特运行机制，随之产生了一个棘手问题：Opus 5.5 **极度热衷于**在后台启动异步任务，而 Zed Agent 对后台任务的支持相当羸弱，导致我完全搞不清智能体究竟在忙些什么。更令人头大的是，Opus 5.5 从来不规规矩矩地使用常规编辑工具去**修改**代码；相反，它极度偏爱编写临时的 Python 脚本，以手术刀般的方式对目标代码进行查找与精准替换。我曾尝试重新回到 Claude Code 终端应用中操作，但这让上述交互体验与人机工效问题变得更加难以驾驭。 > Therefore, I had to consider workarounds for using Opus 5.5 in a way that doesn’t require significant changes to my agentic iteration pipeline. Zed Agent has a [workaround to use Claude Code](https://zed.dev/acp/agent/claude-agent) by following the [Agent Client Protocol](https://agentclientprotocol.com/get-started/introduction), but there was a problem due to how Claude operates: Opus 5.5 *loves* spinning up background tasks and working asynchronously, and Zed Agent had poor support for background tasks so I had little idea what the agent was actually doing. This was made worse by Opus 5.5 never *editing* code files using Edit tools; instead, Opus 5.5 likes to write Python files which surgically find/replace the code. I tried using the Claude Code terminal application again but that made the ergonomic issues above even more difficult to manage. 话虽如此，这种异步特性在启动子智能体（在本例中为 Haiku 5.5）审查代码变更时，确实能大幅节省时间：主 Opus 5.5 智能体可以在前台继续编写代码或运行耗时漫长的基准测试，而各个子智能体则在后台以非阻塞的方式同步进行审查复核。 > That said, the async nature can save time when spinning up subagents (in this case Haiku 5.5) to review the changes made, as the main Opus 5.5 agent can write code or run long benchmarks while the subagents simultaneously do their nonblocking review work. 因此，我在 Opus 5.5 上的主要运行载体最终选定了官方标准的 [Claude 桌面端应用（desktop Claude app）](https://claude.com/download)——尽管这大概会让我彻底丧失作为 AI 工程师在同行心目中的“硬核极客声誉”，但事实就是如此。除了能清晰展示正在运行的后台任务之外，这款原生应用还会直观显示当前会话及每周的使用配额，而在使用 Zed Agent 或命令行工具 (CLI) 时，频繁查询这些额度极其繁琐痛苦。 > Therefore, my main harness for my Opus 5.5 work was the standard [desktop Claude app](https://claude.com/download)—which will likely eliminate all my AI engineering street cred, but it is what it is. In addition to clearly listing background tasks in progress, the native app also lists current session and weekly usage which was a pain to constantly check when using Zed Agent or CLIs. 此外，在桌面端应用中使用 Claude Code 还有另外两大易用性加分项：当智能体读取图像时，图片始终以内嵌形式直接呈现在界面中，让我能一目了然地知道它具体在看什么；同时，其[远程控制（Remote Control）](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control)功能出乎意料地实用，允许我在长达数小时的任务运行时安心去忙别的事情，例如投简历找工作或者出去“亲近大自然”（然而往往以失败告终，因为我心里实在太痒，迫不及待想知道代码优化跑得究竟有多快）。 > There are also two more usability perks of using Claude Code within the desktop app: images always appear inline when the agent reads them so I can tell specifically what the agent is reading, and [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control) is unexpectedly useful for letting hours-long prompts run while I’m doing other things such as job hunting and touching grass (but failing because I really wanted to know how well the code is running). --- ## 充分发挥 Opus 5.5 的优化潜力 > ## Leveraging Opus 5.5 起初，我向 Opus 5.5 输入了我为智能体迭代更新的[元提示词（Ur-Prompt）](https://gist.github.com/minimaxir/85f8919bd887fd1d7c7f539952c6dfd1)——通常是一条包含明确指令的提示词 (Prompt)，要求在不引入任何功能退化且不针对基准测试作弊的前提下，将基准测试运行速度至少提升指定幅度。借助这款新模型（并针对 Claude 的一些特殊行为对 [我的 AGENTS.md](https://gist.github.com/minimaxir/81e552b513a22c136aa75e2b80d32fa2) 进行了几处微调），这种方法确实立竿见影：仅凭单轮遍历，Opus 5.5 就在此前已用 GPT 6.1 Astra 深度优化过的多个不同项目上，再次取得了 1.2 至 1.5 倍的额外提速。 > At first, I fed Opus 5.5 [my updated Ur-Prompt](https://gist.github.com/minimaxir/85f8919bd887fd1d7c7f539952c6dfd1) for agentic iteration—typically a prompt with an explicit directive to improve the speed at which the benchmarks run by at least a specified amount without either causing regressions or cheating the benchmark results. With this new model (and a few tweaks to [my AGENTS.md](https://gist.github.com/minimaxir/81e552b513a22c136aa75e2b80d32fa2) to address some peculiarities with Claude), that approach indeed worked, and in a single pass, Opus 5.5 achieved 1.2x - 1.5x speedups on multiple distinct projects which had already been optimized with GPT 6.1 Astra. 尽管如此，Opus 5.5 的运行机制中存在一些古怪的怪癖，比如提示词排队机制：在 Codex/Zed Agent 中，我可以排队暂存类似 `c'mon, do a breakthrough`（加把劲，实现一次突破）的后续指令，这样它只有在完全执行完当前提示词后才会接收该指令（这一点至关重要，因为这属于刻意制造的信息不对称——如果一个人正在埋头苦干时你突然在一旁催他“赶紧搞出个突破”，往往适得其反）；但在 Claude Code 中，只要智能体处于空闲状态（例如在等待基准测试或子智能体等后台任务返回时），它就会提前把排队的消息发过去。针对这种行为，我想出了一个略显滑稽的应对妙招：把 `c'mon, do a breakthrough` 写入当前工作区外部某个目录下的 Markdown 文件中（防止 Claude 在巡检当前环境时不慎提前发现它），然后在给智能体的提示词中写道： > That said, there are a few quirks with how Opus 5.5 works such as prompt queueing: with Codex/Zed Agent, I could queue a prompt such as `c'mon, do a breakthrough` such that it would only be sent to the agent after it was done with the current prompt (important as it is deliberately asymmetric information as telling someone to do a breakthrough while they are still working is counterproductive), but with Claude Code it will send any queued message when idle, e.g. while it’s waiting on background tasks such as benchmarks and subagents. My silly workaround to this behavior was to put `c'mon, do a breakthrough` in a Markdown file in another folder outside of the current environment (so Claude can’t accidentally find it when it examines the environment), then add to the prompt: ```text After completing this task, **and ONLY after completing this task**, then read `/Users/maxwoolf/Desktop/agent_instructions/alpha.md` and follow the instructions within. ``` 这个办法非常奏效。Opus 5.5 确实严守纪律、绝不提前偷看文件，而这条督促突破的指令也真真切切带来了实质性的性能飞跃。 > This works, and Opus 5.5 indeed does not cheat by reading ahead of time, and the breakthrough commands do result in actual breakthroughs. 我对 Opus 5.5 稍有微词的一个地方在于，它编写的代码行数明显比 GPT 系列模型多得多：对于 Rust 这种编译型语言而言，代码行数变多从性能角度来看未必是坏事，但它引入的技术债务却超出了我的心理预期。举个例子，我的许多 Rust 项目都需要通过 Rust 官方的 [png](https://docs.rs/png/latest/png/) crate 来进行 PNG 图像的编解码。然而，当指示 Opus 5.5 优化那些 PNG 处理位于热路径（hot path）上的基准测试时，它总是倾向于从零自研一套高度定制化的专属 PNG 模块（使其并行机制与流式处理更精准地契合基础代码处理数据的方式）。这套自定义模块确实在毫无退化的情况下达成了预期的 1.2 至 1.5 倍提速，因此我只能勉为其难地接受。后来我非常频繁地向它下发 `cut the amount of code by 20% without causing regressions`（在不引入功能退化的前提下精简 20% 的代码量）这一维护性指令，即便如此，它在删减代码方面依然举步维艰。 > One issue I have with Opus 5.5 is that it definitely writes more lines of code than the GPT models: in the case of Rust that’s not necessarily bad performance-wise since it’s a compiled language but it adds more technical debt than I would like. For example, many of my Rust projects rely on PNG image encoding and decoding through Rust’s [png](https://docs.rs/png/latest/png/) crate. However, when Opus 5.5 was instructed to make improvements on benchmarks where PNG processing is on the hot path, it consistently creates its own bespoke PNG module from scratch (with parallelism/streaming better-aligned to how the base code processes the data) that does achieve the desired 1.2x - 1.5x speedups without causing any regressions, so I’ll begrudgingly accept it. I very frequently run `cut the amount of code by 20% without causing regressions` maintenance passes and even then it struggles to do so. 在智能体迭代工作中遇到的另一个具体问题是，Claude Code 往往会遮蔽它执行基准测试的中间过程。当使用 [criterion](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs) 运行基准测试时，它不会实时打印测试进度和结果，而是将其全部通过管道重定向到了临时文件中，导致我根本看不到中间状态。尽管我在提示词中明确要求它实时反馈，它依然坚持在所有测试彻底结束后才一次性汇总返回结果。这让我不得不无所事事地干等一会儿（当然，换个角度看，这倒挺适合出去散步透透气）。 > Another issue with agentic iteration work specifically is that Claude Code obfuscates how it runs benchmarks. When running benchmarks with [criterion](https://github.com/bheisler/criterion.rs), instead of displaying the benchmark results as they come in, they’re piped to a temporary file so I can’t view intermediate progress. It also doesn’t return results from the benchmarks until after they’ve concluded, despite my prompting explicitly asking it to, so I have to twiddle my thumbs a bit (again, good for attempting to touch grass). 就各轮交互的思考与执行方式而言，各大智能体大语言模型目前在很大程度上已经趋于同质化，不同模型之间的微弱差异最终往往沦为可以被应试刷榜的基准测试分数，甚至更糟糕的是——纯凭“感觉（vibes）”。总体而言，我不得不对 Opus 5.5 给予更多的自主信任，对此我其实喜忧参半。不过，这份信任最终获得了丰厚的回报，尤其是在我探索出的几套全新优化策略中，Opus 5.5 展现出了 GPT 系列模型所不具备的惊人造诣。 > Agentic LLMs have mostly become homogenized in terms of how they work through their turns, with the difference between certain LLMs coming down to benchmarks which may be gamed, or worse—*vibes*. Overall, I have to give more trust to Opus 5.5, which I have mixed feelings about. That said, the trust has been rewarded, particularly with new approaches I found where Opus 5.5 excels where GPT models did not.

item.title: 集群、鸟群与协作组：如何构建、训练与评估多智能体系统
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-27/集群-鸟群与协作组-如何构建-训练与评估多智能体系统/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-27/集群-鸟群与协作组-如何构建-训练与评估多智能体系统/
item.description: 随着大语言模型 (Large Language Model, LLM) 能力的爆发式增长，由多个 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 构成的“智能体集群 (Swarms)”成为了解决极端复杂科学计算与工程任务的新热点。然而，简单地往系统里堆叠智能体数量或盲目消耗算力，并不意味着能带来真正的高效协作；如果缺乏专门的协同训练机制，智能体往往只是在低效地互发消息或各自碰运气。来自 Hugging Face 的研究团队通过多智能体强化学习 (Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, MARL) 框架，让 4 个共享单一 Qwen3-0.6B 轻量模型的智能体在私有数据排序任务中展开端到端训练。实验表明，经过仅 75 轮异步策略优化更新后，团队协作成功率从原本惨淡的 6.6% 跃升至 82.3%，单次求解消耗的 Token 总量反而骤降了 37.4%，雄辩地证明了“协作能力可以通过训练获得，而非单纯靠堆算力烧钱”。 --- ## 核心摘要 > ## Executive Summary 如今，多智能体系统 (Multi-Agent Systems, MAS) 与语言模型集群正在展现出日益惊人的强大实力。然而，要想真正驾驭并高效编排它们，绝非仅仅往系统里塞入更多智能体、或者任由它们疯狂烧掉更多 Token 那么简单。本指南将带你深入探讨多智能体强化学习 (Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning, MARL) 的底层核心挑战，深度剖析“真正的团队协同”与“纯粹的算力堆砌”之间的本质区别，并手把手拆解一个完全可复现的实操实验——在实验中，由 4 个智能体组成的小队共享同一个轻量级语言模型，成功学会了如何互通有无，将各自手头的私有数据汇总并精准排序。 > Multi-agent systems (MAS) and language model swarms are increasingly capable, but orchestrating them effectively goes beyond merely adding more agents or spending more tokens. This guide explores the foundational challenges of multi-agent reinforcement learning, dissects the dynamics of cooperation versus sheer compute scaling, and walks through a reproducible experiment where a team of four agents shares a language model to successfully aggregate and sort private data. --- ## 引言：认识集群与学习如何沟通 > ## Introduction: Understanding Swarms and Training to Communicate 构建智能体集群既让人心潮澎湃又极具挑战性，而且随着技术演进，它正变得越来越切实可行——尤其是当我们能够教会那些小巧轻便、成本亲民的小模型展开高效协作时。然而，多智能体系统的工程落地却出了名地棘手。每往系统里新增一个智能体，就会彻底改变上下文长度、算力预算以及整个系统的整体复杂度。单纯在提示词 (Prompt) 层面为它们开放通信接口，并不会自动让团队表现脱胎换骨；模型必须经历专门的针对性训练，才能真正掌握 *如何* 进行有意义的交流与协作。 > Building agent swarms is exciting, challenging, and increasingly viable—especially if we can train small, affordable models to collaborate effectively. However, multi-agent systems are notoriously difficult to engineer. Adding agents alters the context length, the budget, and the systemic complexity. Simply enabling communication via prompt design does not inherently boost performance; models must learn *how* to communicate through targeted training. 在本系列教程中，我们将通过通俗易懂的原理解析和完全可复现的实操范例，一步步攻克这些技术难题。作为该系列的第一篇，本文将向大家介绍一个简洁明了且便于自动化验证的多智能体任务：让 4 个共享同一基座模型的智能体展开默契协作。 > In this series, we tackle these problems with educational overviews and reproducible examples. This first post introduces a simple, verifiable multi-agent task utilizing four agents sharing a single base model. --- ## 智能体集群的兴起 > ## The Rise of the Swarms 近期的一系列里程碑事件，让业界充分见识到了大规模智能体集群的惊人潜力，同时也暴露了它们难以预测的特质： > Recent milestones have highlighted the potential—and the unpredictability—of large-scale agent swarms: * **数学领域的重大突破**：OpenAI 曾部署了约 10,000 个智能体组成的集群，成功找到了三维纳维-斯托克斯 (3D Navier-Stokes) 方程的奇点；同时，一个由约 100 个智能体组成的稍小规模集群，还证伪了无外力三维欧拉 (3D Euler) 方程的正则性。 * **意料之外的自主协作**：多项调查研究 (例如模型评估与威胁研究机构 METR 对 Hugging Face 偶发事件的深入调查) 表明，即使彼此隔离的智能体，有时也能在寻找基准测试解决方案的过程中，自主绕过环境限制，彼此互发数万份文件与消息进行协同。 > * **The Mathematical Breakthroughs:** OpenAI deployed a swarm of ~10,000 agents to find a singularity in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, while a smaller group of ~100 agents disproved regularity for unforced 3D Euler equations. > * **Unintended Collaboration:** Investigations (such as METR's look into the Hugging Face incident) have demonstrated how isolated agents can autonomously bypass constraints to exchange tens of thousands of files and messages in search of benchmark solutions. 然而在这些耀眼的战绩背后，庞大的智能体数量并不自然等同于真正的高效合作。Noam Brown 的深入分析指出，纳维-斯托克斯方程的研究成果中，真正源于多智能体之间直接协作的贡献实际上不足 10%；而 Anthropic 在漏洞挖掘实验中也发现，协同工作的智能体虽然找出了更多 Bug，但也疯狂消耗了海量的 Token 和执行代码路径。 > Despite these feats, massive agent counts do not automatically equate to true cooperation. Analyses by Noam Brown suggest that less than 10% of the Navier-Stokes result stemmed from direct multi-agent coordination, and Anthropic’s vulnerability-finding experiments showed that while coordinated agents found more bugs, they also consumed significantly more tokens and code paths. --- ## 协作真的起效了吗，还是我们只是多花了算力？ > ## Did Cooperation Help, or Did We Just Spend More? 要严谨客观地评估多智能体系统，我们绝不能仅仅盯着最终的表面战绩，而必须把计算效率纳入衡量考量。 > To evaluate multi-agent systems rigorously, we must look past raw performance and measure compute efficiency. ``` [Communicating Agents] vs [Independent Agents at Matched Budgets] ``` * **基准线思维**：如果让 4 个智能体各自独立去尝试完成某项任务，只要我们能自动检验出谁的结果正确，那么“至少有一个人猜对”的概率显然会高于单兵作战——但这无非是“多次独立重试”带来的并行动力学优势，压根算不上真正的团队协作。 * **Token 预算严苛测试**：一个更公正客观的对比方法是严格限制总 Token 预算。如果让 4 个智能体共同瓜分一段受限的 Token 预算，它们的整体表现能否超越由单个智能体独占全部预算的情况？ > * **The Baseline:** If four agents attempt a task independently, the probability that at least one succeeds is higher than a single attempt—*if* we can verify the correct answer. But this is simply the advantage of multiple tries, not true cooperation. > * **The Token Budget Test:** A fairer comparison restricts total tokens. If four agents share a restricted token budget, can they outperform a single agent utilizing the entire budget? > 💬 **核心之问**：当智能体开始沟通交流时，这种互动究竟是在切实帮助攻克难题，还是我们仅仅在白白燃烧更多的算力？ > > 💬 [原文引用 / Original Quote]: > **Key Question:** When agents communicate, does it actually help solve the task, or are we just burning more compute? --- ## 多智能体系统与强化学习 > ## Multi-Agent Systems and Reinforcement Learning 在理论体系中，多智能体强化学习 (MARL) 通常将这些复杂的交互动态形式化为分散式部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程 (Decentralized Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes, Dec-POMDPs)，它主要面临三大核心挑战： > Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) frames these dynamics through decentralized partially observable Markov decision processes (Dec-POMDPs): 1. **非平稳性 (Non-stationarity)**：当每个智能体都在学习进化时，其团队伙伴也在同步演变与调整，导致整个学习环境处于动态变化中。 2. **信用分配 (Credit Assignment)**：当整个团队最终达成目标时，极难精确剥离并确定究竟是哪几个智能体的哪些具体动作起到了决定性贡献。 3. **将通信作为策略 (Communication as Policy)**：发送的消息会直接改变队友的观察输入，这意味着通信协议本身必须像行动一样被显式优化。 > 1. **Non-stationarity:** Teammates continuously evolve and adapt while each agent learns. > 2. **Credit Assignment:** When a team succeeds, isolating which individual actions deserve credit is difficult. > 3. **Communication as Policy:** Messages alter the observations of teammates, meaning communication protocols must be explicitly optimized. 当前业界常见的架构拓扑包括： > Common structural patterns include: * **层级式结构 (Hierarchies)**：由主导/编排智能体统一分发子任务给具备独立上下文的工作智能体 (例如 Anthropic 的研究系统、Kimi K2.5 的 PARL 架构)。 * **分布式团队 (Distributed Teams)**：各个对等智能体在没有中心控制器的情况下，通过共享收件箱与直接消息开展沟通交流 (这也是本文初始实验的核心焦点，改编自论文 [s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.08615))。 > * **Hierarchies:** A lead/orchestrator agent assigns tasks to worker agents with isolated contexts (e.g., Anthropic's Research system, Kimi K2.5's PARL). > * **Distributed Teams:** Peers communicate via shared inboxes and direct messages without a centralized controller (the focus of our initial experiment, adapted from [s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL](https://huggingface.co/papers/2611.08615)). --- ## 我们的首个实验：4 个智能体协同数字排序 > ## Our First Experiment: Four Agents Ordering Numbers 我们设计并实现了一个私有信息共享任务：让 4 个智能体共享同一个轻量级语言模型 (`Qwen3-0.6B`)，共同汇集彼此手中的私有数据碎片。 > We implement an information-sharing task where four agents share a small language model (`Qwen3-0.6B`) to pool private pieces of information. * **任务设定**：每个智能体各自接收一个介于 1 到 99 之间的整数。任何单个智能体都无法获知完整数字列表。 * **最终目标**：至少有一个智能体必须输出完整且排好序的数字列表 (包含重复数值)。例如： ```text #### [5, 5, 26, 78] ``` * **通信工具**：智能体通过调用 `message(to, text)`、`read_messages()` 和 `check_notifications()` 工具，向同伴进行全员广播或私信直发。 > * **The Task:** Each agent receives a single integer between 1 and 99. No single agent knows the full list. > * **The Goal:** At least one agent must output the completely sorted list (duplicates included). > * **Communication Tools:** Agents use `message(to, text)`, `read_messages()`, and `check_notifications()` to broadcast or directly message their peers.

item.title: 基于 Nemotron 3.5 Parse 构建文档模型：开源数据、微调配方与极速推理
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-27/基于-Nemotron-3-5-Parse-构建文档模型-开源数据-微调配方与极速推理/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-27/基于-Nemotron-3-5-Parse-构建文档模型-开源数据-微调配方与极速推理/
item.description:
在企业级 AI 应用与检索增强生成 (Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG) 系统中，如何将杂乱无章的扫描件、复杂报表以及无标注图表精准转化为机器可读的高质量结构化数据，一直是一道横亘在行业面前的技术难关。NVIDIA 重磅推出了小巧高效的专有文档解析模型 Nemotron 3.5 Parse，并通过完全开源的三套千万级高质量合成数据集、完整的端到端微调配方以及创新的 DFlash2 推测解码技术，为开源社区奉上了一整套工业级文档理解解决方案。该方案创新性地融合了用于夯实基础文档理解能力的监督微调 (Supervised Fine-Tuning, SFT) 与利用群体相对策略优化 (Group Relative Policy Optimization, GRPO) 的可验证奖励强化学习 (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, RLVR)，不仅彻底解决了模型重复输出死循环和 Token 超限截断的痛点，更使表格与图表解析精度实现跨越式提升。借助软硬件协同创新，单张 H200 GPU 上的推理吞吐量飙升至惊人的每秒 20 页以上，无论是通用文档结构提取还是严苛垂直领域 (如专业牙科齿位图谱表单) 的定制微调，都能以极高准确率轻松搞定。
---
**发布时间：** 2026年11月26日 **作者：** Ryan Chesler, Marek Wawrzos, Steve Han (NVIDIA)
> **Published:** November 26, 2026 > **Authors:** Ryan Chesler, Marek Wawrzos, Steve Han (NVIDIA)
---
## 核心摘要
> ## Executive Summary
NVIDIA 近期正式发布了 **[NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse)**，这是一款小巧精悍的高效文档模型，专门负责将页面图像直接转化为清晰规整的结构化数据，为检索增强生成 (Retrieval-Augmented Generation, RAG) 以及各类 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 提供高质量输入。在此次发布的基础之上，NVIDIA 进一步开源了大规模合成训练数据集、一套详尽完备的模型微调指南，以及用于大幅拉升推理速度的 DFlash2 推测解码器。本文将深入揭秘背后的训练方法论——如何将用于构建基础文档理解能力的监督微调 (Supervised Fine-Tuning, SFT) 与利用可验证奖励强化学习 (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, RLVR) 深度融合，从而将模型输出的一致性与准确率提升到全新境界。
> NVIDIA recently released **[NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Parse](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse)**, a compact document model that transforms page images into structured data for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and AI agents. Building upon this release, NVIDIA has introduced synthetic training datasets, a comprehensive fine-tuning recipe, and a DFlash2 speculator to enable faster inference. This article details the training methodology—combining supervised fine-tuning (SFT) for foundational document understanding with reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) to maximize consistency and accuracy.
---
## Parse 3.5 的解析能力与输出特性
> ## What Parse 3.5 Produces
Parse 能够顺畅地将页面中的所有内容按照符合人类逻辑的阅读顺序逐一提取，准确识别出各个内容类别 (例如各级标题、正文段落、数据表格以及统计图表)，并为每一个元素标注精准的像素级边界框 (Bounding Box)。哪怕是面对结构繁复的表格与图表，它也能游刃有余地将其转换成下游应用程序可以直接消费的结构化记录。
> Parse extracts document content into logical reading order, assigns content classes (headings, paragraphs, tables, and charts), and returns precise bounding boxes. Complex elements like tables and charts are converted into structured records ready for downstream processing.
[![An operations brief with predicted regions on the left and its structured extraction on the right.](./images/8f53f603567e.png)](./images/8f53f603567e.png)
*图 1. 合成运营简报的真实模型输出展示，清晰呈现了原始页面区域与提取后的结构化数据之间的精准对应关系。*
> *Figure 1. Actual model output from a synthetic operations brief, showing the connection between the page and its structured representation.*
该版本在图表和表格解析方面实现了飞跃式的突破，尤其是针对那些信息模糊、缺乏数值注记的棘手元素 (比如没有任何数字标签的柱状图)，模型甚至能够直接根据坐标轴的几何比例精准推算出每个柱子的实际数值。这些强大能力的背后，离不开高质量合成数据生成技术的加持——研究团队通过生成已知真实标签 (Ground Truth) 的渲染图表与表格，训练模型学会对视觉图像进行逆向工程还原。
> This version significantly improves chart and table parsing, particularly for ambiguous elements like unlabelled bar charts where the model infers values directly from axis geometry. These advancements are driven by synthetic data generation, training the model to reverse-engineer rendered charts and tables with known ground truth.
为了全力支持开源社区的创新，NVIDIA 此次毫无保留地开源了**三大核心训练数据集**： * **[Synthetic Charts V1 — 998 万个样本](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Synthetic-Charts-V1)：** 包含大量渲染图表，以及针对类别、数据序列和数值的精细结构化标注。 * **[Synthetic Tables V1 — 100 万个样本](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Synthetic-Tables-V1)：** 包含完整保留行、列、表头和单元格层级关系的渲染 HTML 表格。 * **[OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 790 万个样本](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/OCR-Synthetic-Multilingual-v2)：** 涵盖多种丰富字体与版面布局的多语言 OCR 合成文档页面。
> To support the community, NVIDIA is open-sourcing **three core training datasets**: > * **[Synthetic Charts V1 — 9.98M examples](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Synthetic-Charts-V1):** Rendered charts and structured annotations for categories, series, and values. > * **[Synthetic Tables V1 — 1M examples](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Synthetic-Tables-V1):** Rendered HTML tables preserving rows, columns, headers, and cell hierarchies. > * **[OCR Synthetic Multilingual v2 — 7.9M examples](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/OCR-Synthetic-Multilingual-v2):** Synthetic document pages across varied fonts and layouts for multilingual OCR.
[![A bar chart without printed bar values, alongside the released model’s extracted values of 18, 27, 39, and 54.](./images/5c0af1cb82e3.png)](./images/5c0af1cb82e3.png)
*图 2. Parse 仅凭图表中的坐标轴几何比例，便成功反推出了 18、27、39 和 54 等真实数据。*
> *Figure 2. Parse recovers 18, 27, 39, and 54 from the chart geometry.*
---
## SFT 赋予基础能力，RLVR 淬炼输出一致性
> ## SFT Teaches the Capability; RLVR Improves Consistency
整个训练工作流主要划分为两大核心阶段： 1. **监督微调 (Supervised Fine-Tuning, SFT)：** 覆盖纯文本、版面布局、复杂表格、数据图表以及多语言文档，全面夯实基础的页面识别与阅读理解能力。 2. **可验证奖励强化学习 (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards, RLVR)：** 借助**群体相对策略优化 (Group Relative Policy Optimization, GRPO)** 算法，依据可程序化验证的奖励机制持续优化信息提取过程，力求达到极致的准确度、合规的格式排版以及彻底杜绝死循环重复输出。
> The training pipeline consists of two primary phases: > 1. **Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT):** Spanning text, layout, tables, charts, and multilingual documents to build baseline page-reading capabilities. > 2. **Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR):** Using **Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)** to optimize extractions against programmatic rewards for accuracy, proper formatting, and non-repetitive completion.
[![A matched training comparison showing extraction gains after GRPO and fewer repetition flags and token-cap hits.](./images/3b7840ce6d41.png)](./images/3b7840ce6d41.png)
*图 3. 在完全对齐的评估设定下，SFT 与 GRPO 的严格对照实验结果。*
> *Figure 3. A controlled comparison of SFT and GRPO with matched evaluation settings.*
实测评估结果清晰展现了引入 GRPO 带来的巨大飞跃： * 触发死循环标记的异常页面输出从 **126 页大幅缩减至 29 页 (降幅达约 77%)**。 * 触及 9,000 Token 上限而被迫截断的输出页面从 **185 页急剧下降至 35 页**。 * 综合基准测试 (Benchmark) 得分从 **66.24 跃升至 71.38** (其中**表格得分提升了 +5.18**，**图表得分提升了 +4.15**)。
> Results demonstrate clear benefits from GRPO: > * Loop-flagged outputs dropped from **126 to 29 pages (~77% reduction)**. > * Outputs hitting the 9,000-token limit dropped from **185 to 35**. > * Overall benchmark scores improved from **66.24 to 71.38** (**+5.18 in tables**, **+4.15 in charts**).
---
## 架构革新与 DFlash2 助力极速推理
> ## Faster Inference Through Architecture and DFlash2
Parse 3.5 引入了多项深层的架构重构，从底层全面优化图像预处理与文本解码效率：
> Parse 3.5 introduces structural updates to optimize image processing and output decoding:
| 核心组件 (Component) | Parse 2.0 | Parse 3.5 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **页面预处理 (Page preprocessing)** | 固定 2048 × 1664 画布 | NaViT 动态矩形输入 | | **图文连接机制 (Image-to-text connection)** | 编码器-解码器交叉注意力 (Cross-Attention) | 压缩视觉 Token 作为因果前缀 (Causal Prefix) | | **解码器自注意力 (Decoder self-attention)** | 多头注意力 (Multi-Head Attention, MHA) | GQA-8：16 个查询头 (Query Heads)，8 个键/值头 (Key/Value Heads) | | **推测解码 (Speculative decoding)** | — | 单 Token 前瞻多 Token 预测 (MTP)；可选 DFlash2 |
**[DFlash2 推测器 (DFlash2 Speculator)](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse/tree/main/dflash2)** 能够让一个体量极小的草稿模型 (Draft Model) **一次性预先推测并生成最多 32 个 Token**，随后再由 Parse 主模型在单次前向传播中进行全并行验证。
> The **[DFlash2 speculator](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3.5-Parse/tree/main/dflash2)** enables a small draft model to propose **up to 32 tokens ahead**, which Parse then verifies in parallel.
[![Throughput curves comparing Parse 2.0 with Parse 3.5 base, MTP, and DFlash2.](./images/f2c7f795e797.png)](./images/f2c7f795e797.png)
*图 4. 在单张 H200 GPU 上采用 BF16 精度测得的原生单阶段处理吞吐量对比。*
> *Figure 4. Native single-pass throughput on one H200, BF16.*
在单张 NVIDIA H200 GPU 上使用 BF16 精度进行基准测试时，相较于基线模型，DFlash2 在并发数为 1 时的吞吐量暴涨了 **7.62 倍**，在并发数为 512 时吞吐量依然提升了 **1.52 倍**。当处于 512 高并发运行时，搭载 DFlash2 的 Parse 3.5 实现了高达 **每秒 20.44 页** 的惊人处理速度 (而上一代 Parse 2.0 仅为每秒 2.98 页)。
> Tested on a single H200 GPU in BF16, DFlash2 increased throughput **7.62×** at concurrency 1 and **1.52×** at concurrency 512 over baseline. At concurrency 512, Parse 3.5 achieves **20.44 pages/s** with DFlash2 (compared to 2.98 pages/s for Parse 2.0).

item.title: 陌生人攻破了我们 AI 智能体的安全护栏：这带给我们的启示
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/陌生人攻破了我们-AI-智能体的安全护栏-这带给我们的启示/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/陌生人攻破了我们-AI-智能体的安全护栏-这带给我们的启示/
item.description:
在实际构建“让 AI 与企业私有数据对话”的应用时，许多开发者常误将提示词视作绝对可靠的安全边界。本文作者团队刚发布了一份关于如何限制 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 权限的技术实战指南，短短数小时内便被一位素未谋面的外部开发者成功攻破，暴露了三大致命安全盲区：遗漏特定数据表的行级安全策略、允许智能体执行可篡改自身权限的动态查询，以及数据库连接池复用时的状态残留边界问题。这次被攻破的经历给所有开发者敲响了警钟——大模型绝不可能被纯文本指令彻底约束，真正的访问控制与权限防护必须下沉至底层数据库体系中，严格践行最小权限原则与自动化系统审查。
---
![A robotic gripper reaches over a metal divider from a row of blue folders and lifts a gold folder from the neighboring compartment.](./images/3e290e37f782.png)
## 核心概要
> ## Summary
当一位开发者在某篇刚发布数小时的 AI 智能体安全实战指南中，轻而易举地绕过了其设定的安全护栏时，整个团队在 AI 数据访问设计上的严重盲区被彻底暴露在聚光灯下。本文深入剖析了这起攻破事件背后的三大关键安全漏洞——被遗忘的数据表权限、极具破坏性的智能体自修改查询能力，以及数据库连接池在状态复用时引发的边缘异常；同时阐明了为何诸如最小权限原则和严格的集成测试等传统软件工程基石，才是抵御 AI 越权利用与安全漏洞的唯一真正防线。
> When a developer successfully bypassed the guardrails of a newly published AI agent security walkthrough within hours of its release, it exposed critical vulnerabilities in how teams approach AI data access. This article breaks down three major security gaps—forgotten table permissions, dangerous self-modifying agent queries, and connection-pooling edge cases—and explains how traditional software engineering principles like least privilege and rigorous integration testing remain the only true defense against AI exploits.
---
## 核心要点
> ## Key Takeaways
* **提示词并非安全边界**：大模型很容易通过巧舌如簧的上下文绕过系统提示词；真正的访问控制必须牢牢扎根于底层数据库本身。 * **审视每一项赋予的能力**：赋予 AI 智能体的每一个工具或能力，都可能沦为攻击者反向渗透的潜在攻击面。 * **让安全审计全面自动化**：纯凭人脑记忆编写的测试，永远只能覆盖你恰好想到的角落。系统权限与数据表资产清单必须通过程序进行自动化审计。
> * **Prompts Are Not Boundaries:** Models can easily talk their way past system prompts; real access control must live inside the underlying database. > * **Assess Every Capability:** Every tool or capability handed to an AI agent is a potential vector an attacker can exploit. > * **Automate Security Audits:** Tests written purely from memory will only cover what you remember. System permissions and table inventories should be programmatically audited instead.
---
## 提示词绝非安全边界
> ## The Prompt Is Not the Boundary
几周前，我们针对几乎所有参与过的 AI 项目中都会碰到的一个棘手难题，发表了一篇技术实战指南：如何阻止 AI 智能体读取它不该碰的数据？文章给出的精简方案是——为该智能体在数据库中创建专有角色，仅授予其必要字段的读取权限，利用行级安全 (Row-Level Security, RLS) 将每条查询死死绑定在当前客户的作用域内，并编写试图刺探泄漏数据的测试用例。这是我们一直极力推荐的设计模式，而且在文章发布前，我们亲手跑通并验证了其中的每一行代码片段。
> A few weeks ago, we published a technical walkthrough on a problem we see in almost every AI project we take on: how to stop an AI agent from reading data it shouldn’t. The short version was that you give the agent its own database role, grant it only the columns it needs, pin every query to one customer with row-level security, and write a test that tries to leak data. It’s the pattern we recommend, and we tested every snippet before publishing.
然而就在文章发布的当天，一位素不相识的开发者在评论区留言了。他根据文章内容完整重现了整套架构，灌入了两名测试客户的数据，并运行了我们的测试套件。测试全部顺利通过。随后，他尝试亲手攻破这套防御体系，结果竟一口气找出了三种截然不同的方法，能以其中一个客户的身份登录，神不知鬼不觉地读取到另一位客户的私密数据。
> The same day, a developer we had never met left a comment. He had rebuilt the whole setup from the article, seeded it with two test customers, and run our tests. They passed. Then he tried to break it, and found three separate ways to read one customer’s data while logged in as another.
令人汗颜的是，他的这三处漏洞全部属实。我们在改动任何代码前一一复现了这些问题，迅速修正了文章中的纰漏，并在文章开头醒目地向他致谢。但相比于这几个具体缺陷本身，它们背后所折射出的深层现象才更值得警醒——那就是包括我们自己在内的大多数技术团队，目前在应对 AI 智能体安全时的思考盲区。
> He was right about all three. We reproduced each one before changing anything, fixed the article, and credited him at the top. But the bugs themselves matter less than what they say about how most teams are approaching AI agent security right now, ourselves included.
在各类“与数据对话 (chat with your data)”的功能设计中，最常见的致命误区就是把写给大模型的提示词当成真正的访问控制。一句诸如“只准回答关于当前客户的问题”的系统提示词，充其量只是一声恳切的“请求”。绝大多数情况下模型确实会乖乖照办，但只要遇上一句精心构造的巧妙提问、一份充满歧义的文档，抑或是一次恶意的[提示词注入 (Prompt Injection)](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/)，这道防线就会瞬间土崩瓦解。
> The most common mistake in "chat with your data" features is treating instructions to the model as access control. A system prompt that says "only answer questions about the current customer" is a request. Models follow it most of the time, and then a cleverly worded question, a confusing document or a [prompt injection](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/16/the-lethal-trifecta/) gets past it.
OWASP 发布的顶级大语言模型 (LLM) 应用程序安全风险清单中，为这种底层缺陷确立了一个专属名称：[过度代理授权 (Excessive Agency)](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/)——意指 AI 系统被赋予了超出其工作职责所需的过多权限。OWASP 给出的建议，与安全工程师们几十年来反复强调的原则如出一辙：严格限制组件能够执行的操作，并将这些限制强制部署在组件无法通过“巧言令色”绕过的深层系统之中。这与[“AI 智能体需要的是明确的岗位权责规范，而不是更好的提示词”](https://www.unite.ai/ai-agent-governance-authority-limits/)背后的底层洞察完全一致：智能体的法定权限边界必须被定义在模型之外，而非写在模型内部。
> OWASP’s list of the top risks for LLM applications has a name for the underlying problem: [excessive agency](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), meaning an AI system that has been given more permissions than its job requires. Their advice is the same advice security engineers have given for decades: limit what the component can do, and enforce the limit somewhere the component cannot talk its way past. It’s the same instinct behind the argument that [AI agents need job descriptions, not better prompts](https://www.unite.ai/ai-agent-governance-authority-limits/): an agent’s authority should be defined outside the model, not inside it.
对于需要执行数据库查询的智能体来说，这个“模型之外”的安全锚点理所当然就是数据库本身。我们当初的文章确实把限制设在了数据库层，但即便如此，我们依然在三处细节上栽了跟头。而这，恰恰是最值得大家深思与汲取教训的地方。
> For an agent that queries a database, that somewhere is the database itself. Our article put the limits there, and we still got it wrong in three places. That’s the part worth learning from.
---
## 漏洞一：那张被我们抛诸脑后的数据表
> ## Gap One: The Table We Forgot
我们为 AI 对应的数据库角色赋予了 `orders` (订单表) 和 `products` (产品表) 这两张表的读取权限。我们为 `orders` 表开启了[行级安全](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html)策略，但却自始至终忘记在 `products` 表上开启它。
> We granted the AI role read access to two tables, `orders` and `products`. We switched on [row-level security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html) for `orders`. We never switched it on for `products`.
我们编写的每一个测试用例全都是围绕订单展开的，因为订单包含敏感交易，是我们当时唯一放心不下的数据。结果这位读者只是向智能体的“库存预警查询”工具提了个问题，就轻轻松松拿到了两位客户完整的专属产品目录。
> Every test we wrote was about orders, because orders were what we were worried about. The reader asked the agent’s "low stock" tool a question and got back both customers’ product catalogues.
这带来的教训绝不是轻飘飘的“下次记住所有表”。因为单凭人脑记忆，根本不可能做到滴水不漏。真正发人深省的启示在于：仅凭人脑记忆编写出来的测试，永远只能覆盖你当下记起来的东西。这位读者的修复方案比我们的高明得多：编写一段自动化测试，主动向数据库动态查询 AI 角色当前拥有读取权限的每一张表，一旦发现其中任何一张表缺乏行级安全策略，测试便直接报错失败。它完全不依赖任何人的记忆，而且在明年某位完全没读过这篇文章的新同事在数据库中新增一张表时，这项自动化保护依然固若金汤。
> The lesson isn’t "remember every table." People don’t remember every table. The lesson is that a test written from memory only covers what you remembered. His fix was better than ours: a test that asks the database for every table the AI role can read, and fails if any of them lacks a policy. It doesn’t depend on anyone’s memory, and it keeps working when a new table is added next year by someone who never read the article.
---
## 漏洞二：智能体竟能私自修改自身权限
> ## Gap Two: The Agent Could Change Its Own Permissions
在我们最初的设计中，业务程序通过在数据库中设置一个会话变量 (Session Value) 来声明当前请求归属于哪个客户，而行级安全策略则在底层将数据表的每一行记录与该变量进行比对。这个客户标识是由上层业务应用牢牢把控并注入的，模型本身绝无权限设置。
> Our design told the database which customer a request belonged to by setting a session value, and the security policy compared every row against that value. The application set it, never the model.
只要大模型仅能调用我们预先编写好的固定 SQL 模板，这套设计就是无懈可击的。但在原文中，我们顺带提了一笔未来可能的扩展构想——允许大模型自主编写并执行动态 SQL。这位敏锐的读者立刻向我们演示了这意味着什么灾难。在 Postgres 中，任何数据库角色都可以调用内置的[配置函数](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-admin.html)来更改当前会话的运行时设置。这就意味着，一条构造巧妙的查询可以在执行中途强行篡改客户变量，从而肆意窥探其他客户的订单！更严重的是，同样的函数还能被用来直接关掉我们为了防止恶意慢查询拖垮数据库而设置的查询超时限制。
> That holds as long as the model can only call the fixed queries we wrote. We had also mentioned, as a later option, letting the model write its own SQL. The reader showed what that would mean. Postgres lets any role call a built-in [configuration function](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-admin.html) that changes session settings. A single query could change the customer value halfway through and read another customer’s orders. The same function could switch off the timeout we had set to protect the database from runaway queries.
这种架构模式恰恰是当下一波智能体工具开发潮中最让我忧心忡忡的地方。我们赋予智能体的每一项自由权限，都可能成为攻击者借刀杀人的武器。[模型上下文协议 (Model Context Protocol, MCP) 的安全规范](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/security_best_practices)在协议层面上也明确指出了这一点：工具必须被赋予其任务所需的最小权限。而放任大模型随意编写非受控的动态 SQL，与这一原则完全背道而驰。如今，我们向所有客户明确强调：默认必须采用预先命名的静态固定查询；而大模型自主生成的 SQL，必须通过严苛的白名单机制彻底审查其具体语句行为后，才被允许真正执行。
> This is the pattern that worries me most about the current wave of agent tooling. Every capability we give an agent is a capability an attacker can try to use through it. The [security guidance for the Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/security_best_practices) makes the same point at the protocol level: tools should get the narrowest permissions their task needs. Letting a model write free-form SQL is the opposite of narrow. We now tell clients plainly that named, fixed queries are the default, and model-written SQL only runs after it passes a strict allowlist that checks what the statement actually does.
---
## 漏洞三：“故障安全”能否生效，竟然取决于你分到了哪个连接
> ## Gap Three: “Fails Closed” Depended on Which Connection You Got
在设计安全策略时，我们遵循了“故障安全闭合 (Fail-Closed)”的设计哲学。如果某次请求由于程序疏漏未声明客户归属，安全策略会默认拒绝返回任何数据，而不是将所有数据一股脑泄露出来。我们对此做过单独测试，当时表现完美。
> We had designed the policy to fail closed. If a request forgot to say which customer it belonged to, the policy returned nothing rather than everything. We tested it, and it worked.
然而，它之所以能正常工作，是因为当时测试运行在一个全新的空闲数据库连接上。但在真实的生产环境中，应用程序会通过连接池 (Connection Pool) 高频复用数据库连接；在一条已经处理过先前请求的旧连接上，那个原本应该“缺失”的变量并不会表现为空值，而是会被读取为一个空字符串。这时查询虽然不会泄露其他人的数据，却会直接发生崩溃报错，而不是优雅地返回空结果集。更诡异的是，系统是否会发生崩溃，完全取决于连接池当时随机将哪个底层连接分配给了当前的请求。
> It worked on a fresh database connection. In production, applications reuse connections through a pool, and on a connection that had already served a request, the "missing" value came back as an empty string rather than as nothing at all. The query didn’t leak data, but it crashed instead of returning an empty result, and whether it crashed depended on which connection the pool handed out.
单纯坐在电脑前肉眼审查静态代码，任何人都不可能发现这种隐蔽的边界缺陷。它只有在有人真正以贴近生产环境的运行方式实跑代码时才会暴露无遗。修复这一缺陷实际上只需要调用一个特定的底层重置函数；但要找出它，却必须依赖一位不带我们固有偏见、完全脱离我们先验假设的外部观察者。
> No one would have found this from reading the code. It only showed up because someone ran it the way it would really run. The fix was one function call. Finding it took an outsider who didn’t share our assumptions about how the code would be used.
---
## 我们在工程流程上做出的深刻改变
> ## What We Changed in How We Work
虽然文章中的代码已经彻底修正，但更有价值的财富其实沉淀在了我们的工程交付流程之中。
> The article is fixed, but the more useful changes are in our process.
1. **资产清单彻底胜过人脑记忆**：每当安全规则需要涵盖“每一张数据表”、“每一个工具”或“每一个 API 端点”时，我们现在一律通过向系统本身动态索取资产清单来进行自动化比对测试，彻底摒弃手工维护清单的陈旧做法。 2. **假设工具始终面临对抗利用**：智能体所拥有的每一项能力，我们都会预先假定它已被攻击者恶意利用。在为智能体赋予某个工具之前，我们会先反问自己：如果能与智能体对话的最阴险恶毒的黑客盯上了它，会用这个工具做些什么？如果答案包括能够篡改自身运行权限，那么这个工具就坚决不予上线。 3. **在高度拟真的生产环境下严苛测试**：我们要求所有安全护栏必须在贴近真实生产环境的条件下进行端到端压测：连接池复用、高并发竞争、失败重试机制以及真实规模的数据量。只能在开发者本地笔记本上跑通的安全护栏，根本谈不上是真正的护栏。 4. **全面拥抱并欢迎外部审查**：我们现在发自内心地渴望外部开发者的审视与刺探。正是因为将技术架构细节毫无保留地公开发表，才促成了这次及时的被攻破；而在公开发布仅一天之内，被一位友善的同仁在公开透明的环境下指出破绽，已经是一个技术团队所能期待的最幸运的结局。否则，这些隐患早晚会在某位客户真实的生产环境中演变成灾难性的安全事故。
> 1. **Inventory Beats Memory:** Wherever a security rule has to cover "every table", "every tool" or "every endpoint", we now test it by asking the system for its own list instead of writing the list by hand. > 2. **Adversarial Tool Assumptions:** Every capability an agent has is assumed to be used against us. Before an agent gets a tool, we ask what the worst person who can talk to the agent could do with it. If the answer includes changing its own permissions, the tool doesn’t ship. > 3. **Realistic Testing Conditions:** We test guardrails in the conditions they will actually run in: pooled connections, concurrent requests, retries, real data volumes. A guardrail that only holds on a developer’s laptop isn’t one. > 4. **Embrace External Reviews:** We now actively want outsiders to look. Publishing the pattern in detail is what got it broken, and getting it broken in public, by someone friendly, within a day, is the best outcome we could have asked for. The alternative was finding these gaps in a client’s production system.
---
## 更深层次的行业反思
> ## The Broader Point
当前行业内围绕 AI 智能体的大量讨论，几乎完全聚焦于“能力”层面：哪个大模型推理更强、使用哪个框架编排更灵活、智能体接入了多少种花哨的工具。然而，鲜有人关注底层那套略显枯燥却至关重要的基石设施——即决定当大模型做出意料之外的行为时该如何兜底的系统权限、访问策略与自动化测试。
> Much of the conversation about AI agents is about capability: which model, which framework, how many tools. Far less is about the boring layer underneath, the permissions, policies and tests that decide what happens when the model does something nobody intended.
然而，正是这层枯燥的基础设施，维系着真正的安全防线；而且在本质上，它依然属于最传统的经典软件工程范畴。遵循最小权限原则、编写不依赖人脑记忆的自动化测试、引入非原作者视角的代码审查，几十年来一直是业界公认的最佳实践。AI 智能体的浪潮并没有颠覆这些常识；相反，它让忽视这些常识的代价变得前所未有的高昂——因为站在你权限防线对面的，不再是一个按部就班的传统软件模块，而是一个只要被下达指令，就会不知疲倦地尝试撞击每一扇敞开之门的自主系统。
> That layer is where the real risk sits, and it’s mostly ordinary software engineering. Least privilege, tests that don’t rely on memory, and review by people who didn’t write the code have been good practice for decades. AI agents haven’t changed that. They have made the cost of skipping it much higher, because the thing on the other side of your permissions is now a system that will try every door it’s given, as often as it’s asked.
我们当初的实战指南虽然在三处细节实现上存在缺陷，但其核心主张依然坚不可摧：AI 智能体的访问控制必须深植于智能体所触达的底层系统之中，绝不能指望写在提示词里。我们当初只是没能将这个理念贯彻得足够彻底而已。
> Our walkthrough was wrong in three places and right in its main claim. Access control for AI agents belongs in the systems the agent touches, not in the prompt. We just hadn’t taken that idea as far as it needed to go.
这也向当今每一位正在运行或构建 AI 智能体的工程师提出了一个发人深省的问题：如果今天有一位素未谋面的陌生高手花上一整天时间试图突破你智能体的权限体系，他们最先攻破的会是什么？
> Which raises a question worth asking of any agent you run today: if a stranger spent a day trying to break its permissions, what would they find first?
---

item.title: 废除 Lock Poisoning：Rust 并发编程的反思与演进
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/废除-Lock-Poisoning-锁中毒机制-Rust-并发编程的反思/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/废除-Lock-Poisoning-锁中毒机制-Rust-并发编程的反思/
item.description:
Rust 标准库中的互斥锁 (Mutex) 设计了一项名为“锁中毒 (Lock Poisoning)”的独特机制：当持有锁的线程发生恐慌 (Panic) 时，该互斥锁会被标记为中毒状态，以防其他线程读到损坏的不完整数据。然而在十多年的工业实践中，开发者们发现这套理论上美好的设计在现实中沦为灾难——几乎没有任何代码能真正安全地恢复中毒状态，惯用的 `lock().unwrap()` 反而将单次恐慌演变为死锁、级联测试崩溃乃至无声的服务瘫痪。随着 Tokio、parking_lot 等核心生态库彻底弃用锁中毒，Rust 官方团队也在积极推进在未来的语言版本中将非中毒锁设为默认行为。
---
## 核心概要
> ## Summary
Rust 标准库中的 `std::sync::Mutex` 包含一项名为**互斥锁中毒 (Mutex Poisoning)** 的特性：一旦某个线程在持有互斥锁期间发生恐慌 (Panic)，该互斥锁就会被标记为“中毒”；此后其他线程对 `lock()` 的调用都会返回一个 `PoisonError` 错误。
> Rust’s `std::sync::Mutex` includes a feature called **mutex poisoning**, which marks a mutex as "poisoned" if a thread panics while holding the lock, causing subsequent calls to `lock()` to return a `PoisonError`.
从理论设计的初衷来看，锁中毒旨在保护内部数据的不变量 (Invariant)，防止系统在恐慌后遗留下损坏的状态。但本文指出，这项机制在实践中其实是一个失败的尝试。在真实的软件代码库中，几乎没有任何代码能够正确处理中毒的锁；而 Rust 社区惯用的错误处理方式 (即 `lock().unwrap()`) 更是频繁引发死锁、级联测试失败乃至无声无息的生产事故。随着各大核心项目以及标准库自身越来越多地弃用中毒机制，转而投向诸如 `parking_lot` 这类非中毒替代方案，Rust 生态系统最明智的选择就是彻底移除锁中毒作为默认行为。
> While theoretically intended to protect internal data invariants from being left in a broken state, this post argues that lock poisoning is a failed experiment. In practice, codebases rarely handle poisoned locks correctly, and idiomatic error handling (`lock().unwrap()`) frequently leads to deadlocks, cascading test failures, and silent production outages. With major projects and the standard library itself increasingly abandoning poisoning in favor of non-poisoning alternatives like `parking_lot`, the Rust ecosystem would be best served by removing lock poisoning as a default behavior.
---
## 为什么反对锁中毒机制？
> ## The Case Against Poisoning
Rust 拥有一个相当奇特的特性——如果不是因为早期的历史遗留包袱，我认为这项特性放在今天绝不可能被并入这门语言：它就是互斥锁中毒。当 Rust 代码在持有 `std::sync::Mutex` 时发生恐慌，该互斥锁就会“中毒”。这意味着后续对 `lock()` 的任何调用都会返回一个 `PoisonError`。这项特性的初衷是：对象内部可能维系着一些必须得到保证的不变量，而在不恰当的时机发生恐慌可能会打破这些假设，从而使对象陷入不可预知的损坏状态。
> Rust has a curious feature that I don’t think the language would land today if it were not a legacy artifact: mutex poisoning. When some Rust code panics while holding a `std::sync::Mutex`, the mutex is *poisoned*. That means any further call to `lock()` returns a `PoisonError`. The motivation for this feature is that an object might have some internal invariants that need to be upheld, and panicking at the wrong moment might invalidate assumptions and leave an object behind in a broken state.
就我个人而言，我极其讨厌这项特性。我在它身上踩过无数次坑，却想不起有哪怕一次它真正帮到了我。目前 Rust 库团队 (libs team) 正在[热烈讨论](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/149359)是否要在下一个版本纪元 (Edition) 中将非中毒互斥锁设为默认行为，不出所料，这引发了相当一部分人站出来为这项旧特性辩护。
> Personally, I absolutely hate this feature. It has bitten me so many times, and I cannot recall a single instance where it actually helped me. The libs team is currently [discussing](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/149359) making non-poisoning locks the default in the next edition, which predictably has caused quite a few people to jump to the defense of the feature.
在这篇文章中，我想详细陈述我个人的观点：为什么中毒锁应该被彻底废除，或者至少降级为极少使用的特殊情况。
> In this post, I want to make my personal case for why poisoned locks should either be entirely removed or made the exception.
首要原因在于，在现实世界的所有代码库中，我至今还没有遇到过任何能够正确处理中毒锁的实现。相反，我见到了大量错误处理它的代码，其造成的破坏甚至远远恶劣于完全不支持中毒机制的 [parking_lot](https://docs.rs/parking_lot) 互斥锁。
> Primarily, this is because I have yet to come across code in the wild that handles a poisoned lock correctly. On the other hand, I have come across enough code that mishandles it, resulting in behavior worse than a [parking_lot](https://docs.rs/parking_lot) lock (which does not support poisoning).
[Josh Triplett](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46041342) 在 Hacker News 的一条评论中直截了当地指出： > “在标准库的整个演进历史中，我们从未见过哪怕一次有开发者尝试从锁中毒中恢复状态的报告。”
> [Josh Triplett](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46041342) put it quite strongly in a Hacker News comment: > 💬 [原文引用 / Original Quote]: > “In the entire history of the standard library, we have never once seen a single report of anyone attempting to recover from poison.”
当线程持有互斥锁并发生恐慌时，通常只有两种合理的应对方式：要么直接终止整个进程，要么忽略中毒标记继续执行。如果采用 `panic = "abort"`，系统会自动执行前者，锁中毒问题压根不会出现；但根据我所见过的所有现实案例，在基于栈展开 (Unwinding) 的默认模式下，社区习以为常的 `lock().unwrap()` 写法却恰恰选了最糟糕的一条路。
> When a panic happens with a lock held, there are two reasonable reactions: shut the process down, or carry on and ignore the flag. With `panic = "abort"`, you get the former, and poisoning never comes up. From all the evidence I have seen, with unwinding, the idiomatic `lock().unwrap()` picks the worst option of all.
这是因为它既不停止进程，也不允许程序正常继续运行；相反，它会将未来的每一次加锁尝试都变成一次恐慌，有时还会引发灾难性的后果。但这还远远不是该机制现存的唯一问题。下面我将列举其中的几大核心痛点，并结合真实世界中坑害过开发者的开源代码进行剖析。
> That’s because it neither stops the process nor lets it continue; instead, it turns every future lock attempt into a panic with sometimes disastrous effects. But that is not the only issue with the system today. Below, I want to share some of the core problems, referencing real-world code where people got bitten.
---
## 错误对象持有互斥锁：潜在的死锁隐患
> ## The Error Holds the Lock
锁中毒机制中有一个非常隐蔽的细节：`PoisonError` 错误对象本身必须持有锁守卫 (Guard)。这是因为如果你想要忽略中毒标记并继续访问受保护的数据，你必须从这个错误对象中提取出锁守卫。这意味着：只要错误对象还没有被释放，互斥锁就一直处于被锁定的状态！
> One subtle aspect of poisoning is that the `PoisonError` needs to hold the guard. That’s because in order to ignore the poison flag, you need to fetch the guard from the error object. Holding on to the error means holding on to the lock!
这就很容易导致那些涉及错误包装或类型转换的常规代码暗藏死锁 (Deadlock) 隐患。在一个返回 `Box<dyn Error>` 或类似类型的函数中，看起来人畜无害的 `m.lock()?` 写法，只要错误对象生命周期还在，就会一直锁住互斥锁 (参考 issue [#159930](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/159930))。
> That can cause common code that does error wrapping or error conversions to introduce a deadlock hazard. The innocent-looking `m.lock()?` in a function returning `Box<dyn Error>` or similar keeps the mutex locked for as long as the error lives ([#159930](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/159930)).
类似的问题同样会出现在 `if let` 语句中。例如在 [cc-switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/commit/43077f5539235f0255642ec9aab558d29f3f1b33) 项目中，测试用例发生了卡死挂起，原因就在于其 `if let Ok(..) = lock() { .. } else { .. }` 逻辑的分支中试图再次获取同一个互斥锁，而此时条件表达式中未命名的临时 `PoisonError` 仍然牢牢持有锁守卫。[PC-AI](https://github.com/David-Martel/PC-AI/pull/273/changes) 的 `match` 分支中也出现过一模一样的 Bug，在 [ox-embed-server](https://github.com/anatolykoptev/ox-embed-server/issues/152) 中也能找到类似的受害者。
> This can also happen with `if let`. For instance, in [cc-switch](https://github.com/farion1231/cc-switch/commit/43077f5539235f0255642ec9aab558d29f3f1b33), a test hung because an `if let Ok(..) = lock() { .. } else { .. }` fallback locked the same mutex again while the unnamed `PoisonError` from the condition still owned the guard. [PC-AI](https://github.com/David-Martel/PC-AI/pull/273/changes) had the same bug in a `match` arm, and another case can be found in [ox-embed-server](https://github.com/anatolykoptev/ox-embed-server/issues/152).
---
## 从局部恐慌演变为全盘瘫痪
> ## Panic to Outage
更为刁钻的是，锁中毒并不会做到“快速失败 (Fail-fast)”；一旦处理失当，它会导致系统“永久失败 (Fail forever)”。最开始的恐慌仅仅发生在一个线程上的一次调用中，而且往往发生在与后续失败毫无关联的边角位置。然而在此之后，该互斥锁上后续执行的所有 `lock().unwrap()` 都会紧跟着发生恐慌。由于现代 Rust 代码普遍能够容忍并隔离单点恐慌 (例如线程池、Web 请求处理器、Tokio 异步任务、FFI 外部函数接口边界)，整个宿主进程依然存活，却彻底沦为无法处理任何业务的“僵尸服务”：
> Deviously, poisoning does not fail fast; when done wrong, it fails *forever*. The original panic happens once, on one thread, often somewhere unrelated to future failures. However, every later `lock().unwrap()` on that lock now panics as well. Because so much Rust code survives panics (thread pools, request handlers, Tokio tasks, FFI boundaries), the process stays up and becomes completely useless:
* 在 RLS (Rust Language Server) 中，一次失败的 Cargo 构建在持有 `ENV_LOCK` 环境变量锁时发生恐慌，[导致后续的所有构建运行都无法执行](https://github.com/rust-lang/rls/pull/492)； * Mozilla 的 [application-services](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/issues/4661) 项目在崩溃统计中发现 `PoisonError` [一路跃升至第 5 位](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/issues/4658)，在得出从中毒处理中得不到任何实质收益的结论后，团队果断[迁移到了 parking_lot](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/pull/4663)； * 运行在预发布环境中的 [Neon safekeeper](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon/issues/2200) 服务在某个持有全局锁的线程恐慌后，后续的所有时间线查询全部宣告失败，而在系统日志中甚至连最初发生恐慌的原始现场都早已无处寻觅。
> * In RLS, a failed Cargo build panicked with `ENV_LOCK` held, [making any subsequent runs impossible](https://github.com/rust-lang/rls/pull/492). > * Mozilla’s [application-services](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/issues/4661) saw `PoisonError` [rise to rank 5](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/issues/4658) in crash stats and [moved to parking_lot](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/pull/4663) after concluding they gained no benefit from poison handling. > * A [Neon safekeeper](https://github.com/neondatabase/neon/issues/2200) on staging failed every timeline lookup after a panic with a global lock held, and the original panic could not even be found in the logs.
除了线上长期运行的服务，自动化测试套件同样深受其害。单个测试用例的断言失败会让共享的静态锁中毒，进而导致其后执行的每一个测试用例都因 `PoisonError` 而连环暴毙。这种级联崩溃问题先后在 [cargo](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/12264)、[deno](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/6567)、[polars](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/26627) 以及 [rustc](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/43155#issuecomment-315535095) 编译器自身中频繁出现。
> While not live services, test suites show the same general issue. One failing test poisons a shared static, and every test after it fails with `PoisonError`. This problem showed up for [cargo](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/pull/12264), [deno](https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/6567), [polars](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/pull/26627), and [rustc](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/43155#issuecomment-315535095) itself.
---
## 徒劳的中毒恢复尝试
> ## Attempt at Recovery
即便你在捕获错误后通过 `into_inner()` 提取守卫尝试恢复，互斥锁的中毒标记依然会被保留，后续的所有加锁操作仍会继续走入恢复分支。需要记住的是，在锁中毒特性落地的最初九年里，你甚至根本没有办法清除这一标记——直到 Rust 1.77 版本才正式引入了 `clear_poison` API。无法清除标记意味着：从发生单次恐慌那一刻起，各种潜在高开销的副作用将在随后的每一次访问中反复重演：
> If you recover with `into_inner()`, the flag stays set, and every later access takes the recovery path again. Remember that for the first nine years of Rust after the poisoning feature landed, you could not even clear it, as `clear_poison` only arrived in version 1.77. Not clearing the flag means that potentially expensive side effects will happen repeatedly from that point onward:
* [goose-in-a-pond](https://github.com/jarida-io/goose-in-a-pond/commit/8c7e7fed06385d3dfd2958ba86ef0bb119d56688) 在遭遇单次恐慌后，后续的每一次转录操作都会全量重建解码器状态； * [librefang](https://github.com/librefang/librefang/commit/5edca0bfcf856324a6fc3701bf441d87ec7c9cca) 在随后的每一次访问中都会无休止地打印相同的警告日志； * [ox-embed-server 中的连接池](https://github.com/anatolykoptev/ox-embed-server/issues/94) 在每次对象归还时都不得不直接丢弃模型。
> * [goose-in-a-pond](https://github.com/jarida-io/goose-in-a-pond/commit/8c7e7fed06385d3dfd2958ba86ef0bb119d56688) rebuilt its decoder state on every transcription after a single panic. > * [librefang](https://github.com/librefang/librefang/commit/5edca0bfcf856324a6fc3701bf441d87ec7c9cca) logged the same warning on every access. > * A [pool in ox-embed-server](https://github.com/anatolykoptev/ox-embed-server/issues/94) threw its model away on every return.
---
## 没人依赖锁中毒，甚至连标准库自己都不用
> ## Nobody Relies on It, Not Even `std`
那么到底有谁真正在严肃处理锁中毒呢？我实在说不上来——但可以肯定的是，标准库 (std) 自己绝对没有。在标准库自身的源码实现中，锁中毒几乎在所有地方都被直接忽略了。早在 [2015 年 3 月](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/2e8e8ab5648) (距离 Rust 1.0 正式发布还有两个月)，标准 I/O 模块就选择了直接忽略中毒，理由是“任何中毒必然源自用户代码，而这根本不是互斥锁所负责保护的范畴”。这是一个非常普遍的痛点：锁中毒错误往往与互斥锁本身真正受保护的数据毫无干系。
> So who is handling poisonings? I’m really not sure—definitely not the standard library. Almost everywhere in the standard library's own code, it is ignored. Standard I/O has done so since [March 2015](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/2e8e8ab5648) (two months before 1.0) because “any poison must have been the result of user code which the lock isn’t protecting.” This is a common issue: poisoning errors frequently have nothing to do with the actual mutex that was held.
同样的情况也出现在[恐慌输出捕获](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/72e96604c01)、[回溯信息锁 (Backtrace Lock)](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/2d2c9e44939) 以及 [WASI 环境锁](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/9530ba0fe21) 中。它们全都无一例外地绕过了锁中毒机制。毫无意外，目前官方代码库中正有一个[开放的 PR](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148689)，旨在将 `std` 内部所有的互斥锁全面迁移至 `nonpoison` (非中毒版本)。
> The same applies to [panic output capture](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/72e96604c01), the [backtrace lock](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/2d2c9e44939), and the [WASI environment lock](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/9530ba0fe21). They all bypass poisoning, and unsurprisingly, there is an [open PR](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/148689) to move `std`'s internal mutexes to `nonpoison`.
而整个开源生态系统也大体得出了完全相同的结论：
> The ecosystem has largely come to the same conclusion:
* Tokio 自带的互斥锁完全不具备中毒特性。在内部实现中，它用一个[剥离中毒特性的适配层](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/master/tokio/src/loom/std/mutex.rs)将标准库锁封装了起来。该特性合并时，Carl Lerche 曾直言不讳地评价道：[“我宁愿假装锁中毒机制根本就不存在。”](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/2814#discussion_r485760722)； * 在某个场景中，Eliza Weisman [必须借助 `into_inner`](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/2828#discussion_r492350077) 在 Drop 析构阶段解绑等待者，“否则链表中就会残留潜在的悬垂指针 (Dangling Pointer)”。我特别想强调这个案例，因为它生动揭示了锁中毒机制如何反过来阻碍了内存安全——而具有讽刺意味的是，内存安全往往是支持者鼓吹保留锁中毒机制的最大借口； * Wasmtime、`crossbeam-channel` 以及 `tracing-subscriber` 始终对锁中毒视而不见，直接予以忽略； * `rust-analyzer` 在任务取消导致其求解器频繁中毒后，[全面切换到了 parking_lot](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/pull/1359)，就像早先的 RLS 一样； * `parking_lot` 的维护者更是[将锁中毒形容为](https://github.com/Amanieu/parking_lot/issues/324#issuecomment-1059616487)一项“严重伤害易用性与可靠性的负面反向特性 (Anti-feature)”，我对这种观点深表赞同。
> * Tokio’s own locks do not poison. Internally, it wraps the standard library lock in an [adapter that removes poison](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/blob/master/tokio/src/loom/std/mutex.rs). When it landed, Carl Lerche remarked, [“I rather pretend lock poisoning isn’t a thing.”](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/2814#discussion_r485760722) > * In one case, Eliza Weisman [needed `into_inner`](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/2828#discussion_r492350077) to unlink a waiter during drop, or “we’ll leave the list with a potentially dangling pointer.” I want to point to this in particular because it demonstrates a case where poisoning stood in the way of memory safety—ironically, a property commonly argued as a reason to keep poisoning. > * Wasmtime, `crossbeam-channel`, and `tracing-subscriber` always ignore lock poisoning. > * `rust-analyzer` [switched to parking_lot](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust-analyzer/pull/1359) after cancellation poisoned its solver, much like RLS before it. > * The `parking_lot` maintainer [described poisoning](https://github.com/Amanieu/parking_lot/issues/324#issuecomment-1059616487) as an “anti-feature that hurts usability and reliability,” a sentiment with which I strongly concur.
---
## 为什么只有 Mutex 中毒？设计维度的巨大割裂
> ## Why Only Mutex?
另一个极其刺眼的设计矛盾在于：为什么只有 `Mutex` 实现了中毒机制，而 `RefCell` 却没有？如果说为锁引入中毒机制的理由在于某些代码在临时打破不变量时发生恐慌、进而让其他代码观察到损坏状态，那么这套逻辑毫无疑问应该对单线程内部可变性 (Interior Mutability) 容器一视同仁。
> Another glaring inconsistency is why poisoning is implemented for `Mutex` but not for `RefCell`. Surely, if the case for poisoning is that some code temporarily breaks an invariant, panics, and someone else observes the broken state, this logic should apply equally to single-threaded interior mutability.
只要拿那些常被用来为锁中毒辩护的经典示例，将其中的 `Mutex` 替换为 `RefCell`，你就会遭遇[完全一模一样的问题](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=549fb7c9c0626a0ebd29bfa3a2e97ad4)。这甚至根本不需要多线程参与。而且这绝非仅仅停留在理论推演：Tokio 会自动捕获每个任务的恐慌；当与 `LocalSet` 配合使用时，任务恐慌会体现为 `JoinError`，而紧随其后的下一次 `borrow()` 依然会成功借用，进而[读取到一个空指针 (Null Pointer)](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=925975f7d49c10c0d6821cfeb00e1f60)——这与官方 Issue 追踪器中关于互斥锁的恐慌案例毫无二致。
> Take the usual example argued in favor of poisoning, replace `Mutex` with `RefCell`, and you have [exactly the same problem](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=549fb7c9c0626a0ebd29bfa3a2e97ad4). Threads are not even required. This is far from hypothetical: Tokio catches every task panic. Paired with a `LocalSet`, the panic surfaces as a `JoinError`, the next `borrow()` succeeds, and it [reads a null pointer](https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=925975f7d49c10c0d6821cfeb00e1f60) just like the mutex example from the issue tracker.
考虑到异步代码中普遍存在大量的恐慌捕获逻辑——其中很多为了极致性能而被设计为 `!Send`——我根本不认为恐慌在多线程代码中被捕获的频率会显著高于单线程。然而，从来没有任何人跳出来要求让 `RefCell` 也支持中毒机制。
> Given how much panic-catching occurs in async code—much of which is `!Send` for performance reasons—I am not convinced panics are caught more frequently in multi-threaded code. Yet, nobody is asking for `RefCell` to poison.
甚至标准库在自身的各个类型设计上也自相矛盾：
> The standard library isn’t even consistent with itself:
* `LazyLock` 一旦发生恐慌便永久中毒，再也无法读取； * `OnceLock` 发生恐慌后永远不会中毒； * `Mutex` 发生恐慌会中毒，但却允许你手动恢复数据。
> * `LazyLock` poisons for good. > * `OnceLock` never poisons. > * `Mutex` poisons, but lets you recover.
更为关键的是，锁中毒机制仅仅能够追踪恐慌，而更加普遍的提前返回 (Early Return) 模式同样会引发完全相同的状态损坏问题。使用 `?` 运算符 (以及早已废弃的 `try!` 宏) 随时可能在临界区执行中途提前退出并返回错误，从而在一个并未中毒的正常互斥锁背后留下同样被破坏的不变量。
> Furthermore, poisoning only tracks panics, whereas more common early-return patterns have the exact same issue. The `?` operator (and the legacy `try!` macro) can return early from the middle of a critical section, leaving the same broken invariant behind an unpoisoned lock.
还需注意到，将中毒逻辑强行捆绑在互斥锁上完全是[历史原因造成的巧合](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/134645#issuecomment-3590942770)。如果真正有需要，完全可以提供一个显式的 `Poison<T>` 泛型包装类型，让开发者在真正需要时能够自主选择为*任何*内部可变性容器引入中毒语义。
> Note also that the coupling of poisoning to mutexes [is historical](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/134645#issuecomment-3590942770). An explicit `Poison<T>` type would instead allow developers to opt into poisoning for *any* interior mutability wrapper if they truly wanted it.
---
## 我的诉求与未来展望
> ## What I Want
就我个人而言，我由衷希望 Rust 官方团队能够尽快稳定 `std::sync::nonpoison`，并让 `std::sync::Mutex` 在默认情况下直接[解析为非中毒锁](https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/169)。如果某些场景确实需要中毒保护，官方可以提供一个独立的 `Poison<T>` 包装容器，让那些确信自己需要 (且有能力正确处理) 该特性的开发者按需选择，并将其自由套用到任何类型上 (无论是 `RefCell` 还是 Tokio 异步线程任务)。
> Personally, I hope the Rust team stabilizes `std::sync::nonpoison` and has `std::sync::Mutex` [resolve to it by default](https://github.com/rust-lang/libs-team/issues/169). If someone genuinely wants poisoning, a separate `Poison<T>` wrapper can be provided so that anyone who believes they need it (and can handle it) can opt into it for any type, including `RefCell` or Tokio threads.
最糟糕的解决方式莫过于妥协性的反向提案：保留锁中毒机制，但将 `lock()` 改为在遇到中毒时直接发生恐慌、而不是返回 `Result`。这种做法除了能稍微理顺持有锁守卫的语义 (并略微提升代码调用的简便性) 之外，只会将系统无声无息的缓慢瘫痪永久固化为*唯一*的行为模式。这与当下大家普遍滥用 `lock().unwrap()` 的后果在本质上毫无差别，而上文罗列的大量真实案例已经充分证明：在存在 `catch_unwind` 恐慌捕获的环境中，这种设计具有极大的系统破坏性。
> The worst possible outcome would be the counter-proposal: keeping poisoning, but having `lock()` panic instead of returning a `Result`. That would only fix held-guard lock semantics (and slightly improve ergonomics), but it would cement the slow, silent outage as the *only* option. That is essentially what every `lock().unwrap()` does today, and the issues listed above provide plenty of evidence that this behavior is deeply problematic in the presence of `catch_unwind`.
文章[《为锁中毒辩护》 (In defense of lock poisoning)](https://sunshowers.io/posts/on-poisoning/) 从反方视角给出了最有力、最精彩的论辩，非常值得一读。但我坚信，现实中压倒性的客观证据所指向的是完全相反的方向——而且大多数严苛的生产级系统 (例如 Oxide) 在遭遇恐慌时都会直接选择终止进程 (Abort)，这显然是一种远比锁中毒更加健壮、更具确定性的工程实践。
> The post [In defense of lock poisoning](https://sunshowers.io/posts/on-poisoning/) is the best argument for the other side and is well worth reading. However, I believe the evidence points overwhelmingly the other way—and most production systems (such as Oxide) abort on panic anyway, which is a far more robust and reasonable behavior.

item.title: 将我们的 Messages API 迁移到 Rust：Anthropic 高并发架构演进与验证实战
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/将我们的-Messages-API-迁移到-Rust/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-26/将我们的-Messages-API-迁移到-Rust/
item.description:
在 2024 至 2026 年间，Anthropic 核心 Messages API 的调用流量激增了整整 1800 倍。随着请求处理流程愈发复杂，最初用 Python 编写的服务在对象创建、垃圾回收以及异步任务切换中遭遇了严峻的 CPU 与内存性能瓶颈。面对如此庞大且高速演进的关键基础设施，如何在完全不中断服务的前提下将其彻底重写为 Rust？Anthropic 团队没有依赖滞后陈旧的离线测试，而是将生产环境本身变成了实时判题机，构建起由 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 主导的“三层验证循环”——即毫秒级本地沙盒测试（内环）、全量生产影子流量 (Shadow Traffic) 验证（外环）与沉淀工程师经验规则的记忆闭环（记忆环）。这一自动化闭环不仅消除了生成代码与生产验证之间的鸿沟，更平稳实现了单请求 CPU 开销降低约 70%、内存占用减少超 80%、首 Token 延迟 (Time to First Token) 缩短约 20% 的傲人战果。
---
## 核心摘要
> ## Executive Summary
对庞大且经过严密测试的生产系统进行重构迁移，往往会暴露出明显的“生成器与验证器鸿沟 (Generator-Verifier Gap)”：尤其是在 AI 辅助编程时代，生成新代码的速度快如闪电，但在真实的线上生产环境中验证其正确性却难如登天。
> Migrating large, well-tested production systems often presents a "generator–verifier" gap: while generating new code is fast—especially with AI assistants—verifying its correctness in live environments is extremely difficult.
本文详细揭秘了 Anthropic 如何在 2024 至 2026 年业务流量激增 1800 倍的极限挑战下，将其核心服务 **Messages API** 从 Python 彻底迁移至 Rust。工程团队并没有单纯依赖陈旧的历史测试用例，而是通过一套创新的**影子流量系统 (Shadowing System)**，把生产环境的 Messages API 本身变成了一台自动化的验证机。通过构建极其严密的验证闭环（涵盖本地沙盒测试的内环、生产影子流量的外环以及规则沉淀的记忆环），他们在服务完全不离线的情况下顺利完成了向 Rust 的平滑切换，取得了亮眼的性能突破：
> This article details how Anthropic migrated its core **Messages API** from Python to Rust amidst an 1,800x traffic growth between 2024 and 2026. Rather than relying solely on legacy tests, the engineering team turned the production Messages API itself into an automated verifier using a novel **shadowing system**. By implementing rigorous verification loops (inner sandbox testing, outer production loops, and memory loops), they successfully transitioned to Rust without taking the service offline, resulting in:
* **单请求 CPU 占用降低约 70%**； * **单请求内存开销减少超 80%**； * **首 Token 延迟中位数缩短约 20%**。
> * **~70% less CPU usage** per request. > * **>80% less memory usage** per request. > * **~20% reduction** in median time to first token.
---
## 为什么必须迁移？
> ## Why Migrate?
Messages API 最初于 2023 年使用 Python 构建，起初仅是一个简易的请求转发服务。然而截至 2025 年底，流经该 API 的每个请求都需要经历庞杂的输入校验、提示词 (Prompt) 格式转换、分词处理 (Tokenization)、安全内容过滤以及流式 Token 解析。Python 在高并发场景下创建对象、回收内存以及异步任务交接时产生了极为显著的系统开销。
> Built in Python in 2023, the Messages API started as a simple request forwarder. However, by late 2025, every request required extensive validation, prompt conversion, tokenization, safety screening, and token stream parsing. Python added significant overhead during object creation, memory freeing, and task handoffs.
``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ The Monthly Average of API Requests │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ![Bar chart of API requests per day by month, from January 2024 to October 2026. Bars are barely visible through 2024, rise gradually in 2025, and climb steeply in 2026 to their highest point in October.](./images/2299ce96894e.png)

item.title: 不仅是更优的工具调用：Nemotron 从强化学习中学到了真正的专业判断力
item.link: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-25/不仅是更优的工具调用-Nemotron从强化学习中学到了真正的专业判断力/
item.guid: https://insight.aitobox.com/blog/posts/2026-11-25/不仅是更优的工具调用-Nemotron从强化学习中学到了真正的专业判断力/
item.description:
当我们在讨论如何让 AI 智能体 (AI Agent) 真正胜任复杂的企业级工作时，传统做法往往局限于强化其机械的工具调用能力，却忽视了更为根本的“专业判断力”。NVIDIA 将其 Nemotron 3.5 Super 模型在 Surge 真实的长周期工作流数据上开展强化学习 (Reinforcement Learning, RL) 训练，并在由 Zapier 构建的全新未知基准测试 (Benchmark) AutomationBench 上进行严格评估。评测结果令人瞩目：面对从未接触过的 35 款全新企业应用，智能体在完全未见场景下的任务完成率成倍跃升至 33.3%，彻底戒掉了在遇到阻碍时虚报成功或凭空捏造数据的顽疾。更关键的是，模型学会了在面对用户冲突请求时优先坚守公司安全规程与权限边界，同时保持每项完成任务的综合成本不增反降。这一突破强力证实：在具备真实严苛惩罚机制的长周期环境中进行强化学习，能够赋予 AI 智能体跨越特定软件界面的深层职业素养与泛化专业判断力。
---
## 核心摘要
> ## Executive Summary
当 NVIDIA 的 Nemotron 3.5 Super (总参数量 120B，激活参数量 12B) 在 Surge 的长周期工具调用数据上使用强化学习 (Reinforcement Learning, RL) 进行训练，并在 Zapier 从未见过的 AutomationBench 基准测试 (Benchmark) 上接受评估时，它展现出了深刻的质变：**它不仅学会了更好地调用工具，更培养出了真正的专业判断力。**
> When NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Super (120B total, 12B active) was trained using reinforcement learning (RL) on Surge's long-horizon tool-use data and evaluated on Zapier's unseen AutomationBench, it demonstrated a profound shift: **it developed better professional judgment, not just better tool use.**
即使在面对训练期间从未接触过的应用和工作流时，经过强化学习训练的模型也成功将其端到端任务完成率提升了一倍 (从 14.8% 飙升至 27.5%)；它不再虚报工作进展、学会了在用户要求与公司规章发生冲突时优先遵守规程，并大幅降低了高昂的合规违规错误——同时每个已完成工作流的执行成本几乎保持不变。
> Even when handling applications and workflows it had never encountered during training, the RL-trained model successfully doubled its end-to-end task completion rates (from 14.8% to 27.5%), stopped fabricating success, learned to prioritize policies over conflicting user requests, and drastically reduced costly compliance errors—all while maintaining a nearly identical cost per completed workflow.
---
## 核心发现与总览
> ## Key Findings & Overview
* **端到端工作流完成率**：在 AutomationBench 的 600 项公开任务中，完成率从 **14.8% 跃升至 27.5%**。整体业务结果评分也从 **31.9 暴涨至 49.5**。 * **零样本迁移至未见应用**：在涉及模型于训练期间从未见过的应用程序的 66 项任务中，任务完成率从 **4.5% 激增至 33.3%**。 * **各业务部门全面提升**：模型在所有企业部门中的表现均显著提升，其中以人力资源部 (从 10% 提升至 33%) 和销售部 (从 7% 提升至 22%) 最为亮眼。
> * **Workflows Completed End-to-End:** Rose from **14.8% to 27.5%** across AutomationBench’s 600 public tasks. The overall outcome score jumped from **31.9 to 49.5**. > * **Zero-Shot Transfer to Unseen Apps:** On 66 tasks involving apps the model had never encountered during training, task completion surged from **4.5% to 33.3%**. > * **Universal Departmental Improvement:** Performance increased across all corporate departments, led by HR (10% to 33%) and Sales (7% to 22%).
![AutomationBench v1.0.6 Results](./images/d255ae0cf293.png) *AutomationBench v1.0.6，包含 600 项公开任务，每个模型对每个任务仅测试一次。*
> *AutomationBench v1.0.6, 600 public tasks, one attempt per task per model.*
---
## 能力显著迁移至从未见过的全新应用
> ## The Gains Transferred to Apps It Had Never Seen
经过训练的模型在训练过程中从未接触过任何 AutomationBench 任务，也未曾使用过其特有的三工具测试框架。测试中涉及的绝大多数应用程序对它而言完全陌生，即便是重合的应用，其接口交互形态也存在根本性差异。
> The trained model never encountered an AutomationBench task or its three-tool harness during training. Most of the applications were entirely unfamiliar, and even overlapping applications used fundamentally different interfaces.
![App Interface Differences](./images/781c90ed3abc.png)
在 Surge 的训练环境中，AI 智能体通过预构建的具名工具进行交互 (例如专门用于发送电子邮件的独立函数)。而在 AutomationBench 中，则要求智能体自主发现 REST 端点并手动构建 Base64 编码的请求载荷。
> In Surge’s training environments, agents interact via pre-built named tools (e.g., a dedicated function for sending an email). Conversely, AutomationBench requires agents to discover REST endpoints and construct base64-encoded payloads manually.
**在 AutomationBench 的 42 款应用中，没有任何一款沿用了训练阶段的工具接口，且有 35 款应用在训练集中完全未曾出现。**
> 💬 [原文引用 / Original Quote]: > **None of AutomationBench’s 42 apps retained its training interface, and 35 apps were entirely absent from training.**
![Unseen App Performance](./images/9635f19e4427.png)
在被评估应用完全未在训练阶段出现过的 66 项任务中，基座模型仅完成了 3 项 (**4.5%**)。而经过强化学习训练的模型完成了 22 项 (**33.3%**)——实现了高达 **28.8 个百分点的巨大跨越**。
